records.title: I had a good experience with Ciaran
records.text: I had a good experience with Ciaran! Quick responses and friendly demeanor made all the difference. I'm really looking forward to diving into the course.

records.title: Overall great- tutors poor
records.text: General overview the courses are pretty transparent, although I would argue that the assignment topics and the assignment guidelines need syncing up as a lot of times one is saying to do a different amount of answers to the other, which is not only confusing but can cause delays for the student to complete this. Moving on from delays, the turnaround from a query to a tutor to receiving an answer is diabolical, and mostly useless. Just retyping the AC isn’t helpful for some and the point of a tutor is to expand and aid in individuals understanding and learning. Assignment feedback I believe to be okay although can be verging on cryptic. But the tutors are not tutors. They just type a blunt response then close the conversation so you then have to reopen a new conversation potentially off the same query.

records.title: I like that i am able to study from…Hit and miss
records.text: I like that i am able to study from home at times that suit me. As a single parent this really helps. I also like that i can contact the tutor anytime and receive fast responses, plus the student forum so you can post a question and discuss with other students. That said, the tutor sometimes gives conflicting responses, and doesn't answer the question but seems not to understand. Some of the quiz questions are misleading, with not stating what format to answer, so when you put 600, the answer is 600.00 or the other way round.

records.title: Course is Not enough to pass an exam
records.text: I was doing AQA Business A Level. The course looked good, my advisor was really friendly the whole time and responded my questions quickly.I had 10 assessments to do and almost all of them was over 80%, she said I was doing great.Then I had my exams in may, 3 all together. I felt I was doing great and I was waiting for a positive outcome.I barely passed the test!!!!! 😡Then I checked the reviews and I saw that I'm not the first one and most of the people don't even pass it or just barely.You should really update or improve the content of your learning materials cause you are wasting peoples time and money.Spent nearly £1k and now it's all wasted.UPDATE: I was talking to a lady on the phone after this review, she was really helpful and she offered extra help for next year in case i decide to continue learning with them. Unfortunetly i have no place to take exams as a private candidate so i couldn't take this opportunity, but i really appreciate the support. I also got partly refunded.

records.title: Average
records.text: Support can definitely be improved. It tales 2-3 days for someone to come back to you and there is very little input from the tutors. They just refer back to the unit guide so when you struggle and are getting close to your assignment deadline, it is difficult to get any support from them. Once they closed the assignment submission function for 2 weeks due to website maintenance. Will try a different provider next time.

records.title: Overall not a bad experience
records.text: Overall not a bad experience. I did request a call to begin with and asked for the call 2 times but nothing came and then my course advisor just kept emailining me. The process was a little all over the place and I would ask that the course advisor actually provides a call if requested by a potential student so you know you are talking to a human. Otherwise, It was an okay experience.

records.title: Hit and Miss
records.text: Some things were great about learning with ICS Learn, like the user friendly website design, the marked assignment feedback, and a few other things. On the whole, however, I didn't feel as though the way it worked got the best out of me. The nature of the online "lessons" is such that you find yourself breezing through things very easily. You need to do a lot of studying outside of the online course material to really embed the concepts in your mind. This is where I think ICS Learn falls short. I found myself using all kinds of resources outside of my ICS subscription until I got to a point that I stopped using ICS altogether. In short, some people may find this format to be really useful but I didn't think it was great. Indeed, I found a very popular private and YouTube tutor whose subscription service was cheaper and whose lessons and resources I found a lot better.

records.title: Value and Trust
records.text: The key point is the Flexibility and affordability offered by the course. The pricing is set reasonable, but going forward to the course I feel to be left alone to gather your own knowledge. You are more exposed to study material and videos.Michelle Kerr, Thanks for your guidance on setting my course.

records.title: accessibility is good!
records.text: extended my course for free with a supportive letter from my doctor when i could not do the course for a while because of poor health. the customer service is great! i didn’t feel completely supported and unfortunately i could not complete the course, as my extension ran out. paid a lot of money for nothing, but that’s not fully their fault. edit: i don’t know when my last correspondence was but it was within the last year! my course expired in july, that’s what the date is for

records.title: Good, if you don't have any questions about your course or study!
records.text: The most important thing is the content of the course is good. The results came back quickly and i was able to progress. However, when i had questions about moderation dates, where to find student info, etc the Service Delivery team in the UK were not helpful. In 4 seperate cases they could not, or would not, respond to my questions which was really disappointing.

records.title: Distance learning is new for me
records.text: Distance learning is new for me, I called up ICS Learn to find out more about how to proceed with the course and felt my questions were not answered effectively. The advisor was very nice and polite but at the end of the call I was still unsure of the best way carry out the home study.

records.title: Lacked support
records.text: I did prince 2 foundation and practical, which i passed. Course content put together by Frank Turley is pretty decent, for the foundation. However, support is rather lacking. A week before my foundation exam i requested a call with my mentor. my mentor messaged me on a friday afternoon, a day before my exam, telling me he will not call me and he is about to go on leave. if there a any issue to just message him. What good is that when it takes 5 working days to respond?! Additionally, learning support mostly ignored my messages, i would have to follow up to get a response. I found the practical course ineffective for myself, which may just be me so i just went straight to doing exams and using results to focus on my weaknesses. Knowing that the mentors are to stretched to give specific feedback (at my request, ICS did swap my mentor who responded MUCH faster), i bought a £10 course on Udemy. That course just taught exam strategy and was VERY helpful. have to give credit to them for my success. any questions I had were responded to same day! In summary, if you are a learner who can learn well on your own, including solving issue by your self if you do not understand something, ICS may be a good option as it offers one of the cheapest rates. If you go with them, my advice is find a proper exam simulator, like the one people-cert offer, or buy a cheap udemy course that will offer very in-depth mock exam feed back.If you struggle with concepts and need hands-on mentorship, forget it, as I suspect the mentors are not given the facilities and are far to stretched to give hands-on time.This is my honest review as a passing student. If anyone at ICS is reading this, Please improve your exam quizzes with far more robust explanations for the practical exam it currently feels very half-baked and sometimes conflicting.

records.title: Mixed Experience
records.text: I have just completed a level 7 CIPDGood points:*I purchased my course late Oct/early Nov and when they slashed the price for Black Friday I challenged and they honoured that for me.*3/4 assignments marked within 48hrs*I was able to change my module selection mid course, it was quick and easyNot so good points:*Course content is of mixed quality, one module just basically just said read the textbook, other parts were old.*1/4 assignments took too long to mark*You need to pay to extend your content access*Don’t automatically process your completion you need to contact student services.Overall glad I did it and ICS are fine, points above are to help manage expectations

records.title: Difficult, not straightforward
records.text: I found the process of enrolling with both ICS and CIPS confusing.  It was definitely not straightforward and some of the instructions provided by ICS on registering for CIPS on their website did not work and the pages / links were no longer live.  It took a number of days to navigate the sign-ins and get set up despite watching the introductory videos/assist and going onto the blogs etc.

records.title: Finish your course in 6 months or else it costs....
records.text: i am very disappointed that once your support period is over you no longer have access to your course - this was not very clearly highlighted. So in fact you do  not "buy" the course - you rent it..... and if you dont finish it within 6 months - you have to pay £40per month to extend..... Life happens and I was not able to complete my course within the 6 months, I also dont have cash lying around to extend, so money down the drain for me .... Had recommended this to a colleague but will advise they shop for alternative options

records.title: Sorry but I can’t give more stars … I…
records.text: Sorry but I can’t give more stars … I can actually give ICS 2.5 * Contact and help is perfect but the thing is with materials provided - not enough examples to show, not enough quizzes and tests to do - after doing 1 module I am not ready to Book my exam! I am sure there is no chance to pass it :( the course doesn’t include a hard copy books which you can have from different providers for very similar price and this is very important- TO DO as much practice tests as possible! Ive just done the first example of assessment at AAT web and I can see how poor are all materials and examples delivered by ICS … Dear ICS - please review your materials and add many more test’s and quizzes  because the beginners will never pass their assessment after your course 🥺😢

records.title: The presentation of the material is not…
records.text: The presentation of the material is not very user friendly, If issues with WiFi I am unable to access my materials, I am planning to go away for 2 weeks and access to WiFi will be none, so I can't take any materials with me to work on. It is unaware of how I am progressing through the material, will be helpful if there is indication of percentile covered or further info. On first day I had to wait 2-3 days because system removed all materials. Unless I have a big screen available I am unable to do my assessments, even with a laptop I was unable to do some of the tasks during the assessment.... Moving sentences, but screen not big enough to allow me to do this. So I left some questions unanswered which did affect my result.

records.title: Some Markers are EXTREMELY Temperamental!
records.text: I won't recommend ICS for online qualifications, and I wish I didn't choose it for my studies.I am currently studying CIPD Level 5 in L&D.Main points:- Painfully slow feedback that can take up to 10 weeks.- Support is just a word, no real problem-solving.- Feedback from some tutors is just useless.I have passed 5 units and 2 more to go, however, I keep getting referred for very trivial issues and for some ACs for very illogical reasons such as a marker changing his/her mind about an AC that she passed me in my first attempt and fails me in my second!I would not recommend ICS for anyone.Update: I thought they would consider fixing this or at least contact me, but the reality is...they just don't care even after they saw the rating and feedback...Update #2: Finally, I received an email from the Head of Curriculum, she did show genuine care about my issue and refunded me a previous payment, and gave me a 3-month support period for free as a token of goodwill. This is what i was looking for, a person who really cares and communicates properly and listens to what challenges students are facing and provides adequate solutions.I have passed in the end.

records.title: Not sure if I can recommend it
records.text: My current tutor is very helpful but last year I had an awful tutor who (instead of helping me)  just was confusing even more.Lots of mistakes in their materials which are very confused.Not enough practice tasks after specific topics, they use always a super easy example ( 1 only) and moving forward. On the exams we have much more difficult questions so ICS material is not enough to sat the exam. They do not provide paper books what you can get from a different provider for the same money.I had to buy books because like I said above the provided material is not enough to pass the exam.I think the next time I would pick a different provider.EDIT after receiving the answer:I reported many times that provided material is NOT ENOUGH to pass the exam but every time I heard the Same : it is enough..this is your opinion but mine is different.I wouldn't pass my exams without paper books support Every time I tried to report any issues I found and everything has been rejected by you so what is the point to waste my time again?!I gave up some time ago .... Everything looks great that you try to help us etc...but if I report my concerns - everything has been rejected so far  🤷🏻‍♀️

records.title: I have completed AAT level 2 and 3 with…
records.text: I have completed AAT level 2 and 3 with ICS Learn,though i have chosen to buy the 2 together on a deal i wish i hadn't. their course material is somewhat confusing and with many mistakes.i have to say costumer services are are friendly and helpful when needed. Tutors, i used them very few times and didn't see the need really that much. i did got through the slides and activities, but with many mistakes it kind of threw me at times. i concentrated on out sourcing tutorial on you tube and Free FI videos which where much more helpful. their Videos were poor quality and really did put me off so much so that i had a 2 months break from it. AAT [practice tests were extremely useful and the Facebook support group also to be part off, through any question and loads of people will help.All in all, it is ok, but i can't decide i actually hated the experience and at the end i just wanted to be done with it, off to level 4 now with someone else. definitely.

records.title: Prince 2 foundation and practitioner
records.text: Prince 2 foundation and practitioner. My 3 star rating is for my tutor really as he was brilliant and a credit to ics learn. The course content wasn’t engaging at all, full of grammatical errors which is off putting, you watch video after video of Frank Turley in the foundation level which wasn’t too bad but the practitioner level involved being a third party listening to Frank and another chap who practiced a different project management methodology who would frequently start talking about something completely unrelated to Prince 2, I was tearing my hair out. I purchased the manual and it’s basically 400 pages of complex project management with no engagement for the student, having not come from or done project management before I did struggle! The online tests were quite good although again errors and answer options repeated a couple of times in a question, you also get 4 sample  tests too.  Having said all of that I did pass so super chuffed that I’ll never have to do again! IM not sure if other online providers will be any better??

records.title: Everything
records.text: Geoffrey ojok

records.text: NEW CUSTOMER- ENQUIRY I just called customer services to potentially enrol not impressed. Still searching. records.title: Shambolic, so far.
records.text: Lots of issues signing up. Wouldn't let me confirm my payment, and then when I eventually did pay, I got a message from my bank stating that the payment had been declined because "the merchant has processed it incorrectly". When I finally got it sorted, I received an email with important information missing, such as "your student number is *empty space*". Now, I'm trying to start my course, but I can't, because it says the program doesn't start for another year. I hope the rest of the course isn't as shambolic as the start has been.

records.title: Not told after 3 years I would have to pay more money
records.text: Just passed my prince2 qualification that I paid almost £500 for. At no point was it mentioned that the qualification only lasts for 3 years, then you have to retake the course. I only found out when I received my certificate,  If this was pointed out to me I would not have done it and chose another course instead. I was happy with the training provided by ICS but booking in the exam was not an easy process, this was the fault of People cert

records.title: AAT level 2 was great, but level 3 is so bad.
records.text: AAT level 2 was great, but not impressed when i took aat level 3.Response was very slow, took many days to get questions answered, and almost always missed some questions i asked, for example, i asked 2 questions but only got one answered while it still took one week to answer. Some questions I asked in regarding to mock, was answered days after my real exam (5 days later). Doing level 4 now with other institution, so far, my questions were answered within hours.Would not recommend.

records.title: Disappointing once fees paid
records.text: ICS learn sales team are super efficient and communicative following up by text, call and email, they are also quick to ask for review at this point for which I gave five stars to Michelle. Content is good however support or responses from tutors or student support are very poor (I emailed Wednesday and have still not heard by Saturday) when asking a tutor for support and guidance I was referred to their content and chat closed. Wouldn’t recommend if you’re looking for an interactive education experience.

records.title: Course content has errors in
records.text: Course content has errors in, payment plan isn't fully explained and unforseen costs incurred and when questioned all you get is "you docusigned the plan on x date". They won't liase with the exam body on your behalf at all. The recorded sessions of the live lessons that you are meant to have access to and is one of the main reasons that I went with them, are not available for the new courses and are not going to be. Working full time I cannot access the live lessons as they are during working hours! Online free help to learn is often presented in a more understandable way and in a better format.The only good thing I'll say is often the assessment checks and mocks are harder than the actual exams, so when your tutor says to take the exam from a good mock score, you should be more than ready

records.title: Excellent sign up, but no support when it was needed
records.text: Excellent sign up and advice given during this process. However soon after I had a major change in circumstances and wanted to pause the program whilst I mended, I was told under no certain terms could I do this. Are some time and HUGE anxiety about starting, no contact from anyone (ever? Where are the personally assigned tutors?) and I’ve logged into the platform a handful of times and paid £5k for the pleasure.ICS seem to really like to take your money, give you a dashboard and a forum (with other paid users, not tutors) and leave you stranded when you really need support.I couldn’t recommend this company, which is a shame because the initial contact was excellent.EDIT: After the reply from ICS, I’d really like for the customer advisor to read my review and the problem and reread their reply. It’s not about self directed learning, but the lack of compassion or empathy for those who need to pause or ANY form of check in from the tutor (or anyone) when asking for help.They have completely missed this point (which seems to be the case having read other reviews) this is the exact standard of service to be expected whilst attempting to complete your course.

records.title: Not getting responses
records.text: Not getting responses Multiple time asking for payment linkvery poor service from Paul O’Rourke

records.title: Overly critical and inconsistent tutor feedback from several tutors / timelines not told about
records.text: Uploaded an assignmemt and the tutor took almost 2 months to give me feedback, ive uploaded it several times and keep being told to improve the questions i failed on, but they are of the same quality as the others i passed on. very loose feedback and seems overly critical and you have several tutors marking it so different opinions on it which is hard to keep up with. You should grade the assignments overall not fail the whole module if 1 or 2 questions dont meet the criteria of several tutors who provide general feedback that you are then left to figure out. They told me i could study at my own pace then i found out they had put a deadline of his year in dec on it which will be hard for me as i work full time. im now panicking, nobody to chat to i contact my tutor and another random person came back so theres no consistency. I would like my money back and id go with another provider its awful and ha caused me so much stress

records.title: Great value for money & content
records.text: Thank you so much for providing such life changing content! I have recently completed the Child & Adult Sexual Exploitation CPD certification to better my understanding of how children and adults are targeted for sexual exploitation. There were things I already knew due to my personal experiences with sexual exploitation and things I learnt that I had no idea about. The CPD only took me 4 hours to complete yet the knowledge will stay with me for the rest of my life. In a world where predatory behaviours are becoming more socially acceptable it is important to keep up to date with the techniques used to manipulate both children and adults into sex work and exploitation. Thanks a lot for making safeguarding accessible.

records.title: My experience so far

records.title: Great support but training provider has areas to improve
records.text: As a career changer looking to go into project management, I was apprehensive about what qualifications to take suitable for me, how to break into the market and getting industry information. I decided to go with Learning People as I felt they provided all these things, came across as very professional and reasonably priced. Reviews seemed to reinforce what I was looking for.Overall, I am happy with my experience as I have met my objective - got a great new job, competitive qualifications and confidence on how the market operates.My main issues were with the training provider that LP decided to go with. I have raised this with them already, but generally, I felt ILX, the training provider, was lacking in the extensive qualifications (in particular, AgilePM practitioner and APM PMQ).Main issues: - I was expecting when I paid for the package that everything would be included, but was disappointed that textbooks that IMX referred to were not provided. One of my exams was an open book exam, so I had to pay additionally for a textbook to support me.- In the multiple choice exams, there were plenty of exam style questions. In exams which had more complicated formats/written answers, there was very little provided. One practise paper, and for APM a handful of exam questions with little feedback. I had to look elsewhere for additional resources. - Communication from ILX was poor, often taking much longer than expected and I had to involve LP once in order to receive a response. There are meant to be course tutors, but they don’t actually provide much 1-1 support. I acknowledge I took on some of the more difficult qualifications and with that, there should be challenge, but I do think these are quick fixes that would improve everyone’s experience.Overall, I think LP are putting in lots of interesting features to their programs and will provide an easy package for career changers. I fear if you are looking to do some of the more intensive courses, rather than introductory ones, you may be on your own a bit more in terms of support with your learning. I do believe LP listen to feedback though and I hope my response will help them improve.

records.title: Happy customer
records.text: I an happy with my experience from the Learning People. I registered for the AgilePM course and with the help and encouragement from Mikki I have managed to pass my first exam.My reason for not giving a 5  is that you cannot call your representative but via email and there have been a few times when I've been waiting for callback catch ups which have been missed.

records.title: I enjoyed the student support team
records.text: I enjoyed the student support team and career services, they’re ready to put you through your journey till you get your dream job. I am currently working on my LinkedIn page and done with three of my exams out of four, the career services helped me put my cv in order and the student support system in passing my exams. They sent me materials to guide me and I liked the fact that they always check in on you to see how far you’ve gone and any help needed

records.title: I've had a great experience with Learning People
records.text: I've had a great experience with LearningPeople. The courses are well-structured and the platform is easy to use. The exam simulator was a key tool in helping me pass, as it mimics real exam conditions, improving both my confidence and time management. Combined with flexible learning, this platform is perfect for exam prep and skill development. Highly recommend!

records.title: My journey to cyber security…
records.text: I started my journey to cyber security two months ago and it has been a great one because I have learnt a lot. Furthermore, I like the structure of the lectures. Hopefully, I will be able to complete my journey towards Cyber security with learning people. Learning people in general have been very supportive.

records.title: Celebrating a great Team
records.text: I made bold to say that personally,there's no better team to be in than the Learning People Team especially when studying and preparing for the PRINCE2 exams (Foundation and PRACTIONER). These selfless people always keep you on your toes because they want to see you achieve success throughout the Project Management Course. I came in as a complete novice, but today, I am a certified Project Manager (PRINCE2 Foundation and PRACTIONER)😀😀.@Learning People and @StudentCare, please keep the good job you are doing.

records.title: I would advice anyone that want to…
records.text: I would advice anyone that want to study with LP, they should know the course they want to do and not let any of the rep talk you to do about 3-5 courses, which will become a problem. And everything should be well defined at the beginning. They attach the condition that you'll have to pass your exam before you're passed onto a career advisor.. Personally, I think this is wrong because I think assisting their students to have a better career should be prioritize over having passed exam because I've realized to even pass most of the exams, you must be working in the field or at least have a good work experience in the field because the curriculum offered by LP + the exam simulator may not necessarily help with the exams. I hope this review helps anyone interested studying with LP

records.title: ILX Dashboard
records.text: I used all the materials available on the ILX Dashboard, which were helpful overall. However, I noticed that some important topics were missing that only came up when I started practicing with the APMG sample exam papers. I believe it's essential to include these topics in the ILX materials. As a student, it’s easy to assume that all exam-related content is covered, and with limited time, it's not always feasible to search elsewhere. Adding these missing elements would make the ILX resources more comprehensive and better prepare students for the exam

records.title: Its all up to the work you put in!
records.text: The course gives you all the information to kickstart your career in Data, whether it is in analytics, science or DBM. Some of the material is quite outdated and it can be confusing to grasp when operating on a newer system especially on a MacOS system. In my experience, they have readily available consultants and a good option to use mentors, and they have classes which I did not find all too helpful. Ultimately, you get out of the course what you put in, as it is self-taught.

records.title: Like a box of chocolates
records.text: The course materials are great, thorough and organised to make learning an easy process. The information isn't being gate-kept and you can simply download all of the materials for later use if need be.You get assigned a help desk person, in my case it's Jess, whose job it is to keep you on track and be on hand to answer questions and so on. When I wasn't making any progress she'd give me a nudge and she'd promptly organise the exam vouchers when requested.My main issue is with the career services team.What got me to buy into the service back in summer of 2024 is the claim that "98% of our learners find a job in the industry" and the fact that they are launching or already have launched a career services team to help you with your personal brand and the job search. So far, this service proved of no value after well over a month and I'm feeling like I should have saved my money and gone with one of their competitors at a cheaper price.

records.title: While they are a good company and have…
records.text: While they are a good company and have all the facilities set up. I just did not have the support for remote learning and felt I was miss-sold what it would be like; as it turns out my facilitator then left the company. I asked about renewal quotes and there was back and forth and they wanted a chat on the phone when it would have been simple enough to send a quote on email. Just be mindful you'll be left to it.

records.title: The Extras are Good but course content is poor
records.text: I think the extras are really good the support and the career services but that actually course content is rubbish.  It missed massive amounts of information needed for the exam and the app never works. I learnt more from YouTube and I bought my own book. The unlimited resits are good as it take the stress off and the practice system is decent too.

records.title: Good service, might be better off just teaching yourself
records.text: The online learning portal is pretty good. I did the Prince 2 Foundation, Practitioner, Agile and PFQ. I only had a year to do it and they gave me a couple of months extra. I only just managed to achieve this, I think they should give longer access or if an extension is needed I'd hope they'd give longer. I paid around £2300 for all the above courses, however, it probably would have been significantly cheaper just to have bought textbooks, you have to read them and everything needed in the exam is on there. Not sure how much of what I studied I'll actually use, I'm not a project manager but I thought it might be useful to a civil engineer. They check up on you every now and then to see how you're getting on with the learning.

records.title: Need admin to disable programs - exam delayed 30 mins
records.text: The exam software could only run 10 mins before exam time and found a program that needed to be closed. Only a work administrator could disable the program and took me 30 mins to get someone from IT to do so. Having the knowledge about this much earlier would have helped and not make me worry that I would lose exam time. The proctor allowed me extra time, but all of that could be avoided.

records.title: Not for Everyone
records.text: The resources they provide via Percipio are good. PDFs of books, videos, mini tests for each module also mock examinations. The agents check in every now and then to see if you ready to take your exams.The only area I believe they lack is student support, as a student who has ADHD and dyslexia I struggled to keep up with studies. Even when we came up with solutions to help. The agents were not consistent with weekly check-ins and the resources they provided were quite poor (e.g. weekly study planner grid; if I can I'll attach the the document they sent. Quite poorly made) I would only recommend this course to anyone who is really good at independent study and absorbs information quite easily, because when it comes to providing accessibility assistance and screening students who may need it, they fail.Imagine paying £60 a month for 3 years (still paying it off until this day) to only have access to resources and unlimited exam retakes for a year. And you have to complete 3 courses in a year. In my case it was CompTIA+, Network+ and Office. I'll let the public decide if that's good deal or unrealistic and shooting yourself in the foot.

records.title: I passed the comtia exams but with the…
records.text: I passed the comtia exams but with the help from other providers ... sad to say....because i am paying a lot of money.I am traveling a lot and percipio app works 30% of the time. I have tried a different phone ... same think is happening.... so I bought  comtia a+ from udemy ( around £40). Working perfect on my mobile. Now mentioning comptia a+ learningpeople labs... they are trouble. (learningpeople knows already) I am on networking now. For now is ok ...except the app which still not working all the time and giving me a lot of headache....don't know what do.. realy. I will come back with a review on networking labs.

records.title: Great people - good content - terrible labs.
records.text: The greatest asset to Learning People are the people who work there, from the student care to career services team, it feels like they genuinely care for your success and were a pleasure to work with. The content was OK - The app allows for the lectures to be listened to in a podcast style which made studying easier. However some the lecturers were incredibly monotone and boring the only way to get through it was to play it at 1.5x speed. The practice tests provided were good to get you ready for the official exams. There are free YouTube videos that do the same job for A+, Network+ and Security+ , but going through LearningPeople keeps you accountable and motivated since you have paid for the course. Now the really bad. The Labs for APAC are horrible. They are really poor and the servers are set in the US and EU. This makes doing them unbearable. The constant delay and slow times really brings the score down, I can't comment how they are for EU and US customers but they need an alternative for APAC students. Even though I used multiple sources to pass all my exams I would probably use LearningPeople again, just because the workers were amazing.Staff 5/5Lectures and practice exams 4/5Labs 1/5

records.title: Clear and Concise
records.text: I liked my induction to the course, it was brief and to the point much less than 30 min. my questions were answered in the call. I gave it 3 stars because I would have preferred a teams interactive meeting.

records.title: Great job hunting services ok experience with course and exam..
records.text: Great learning services and in my experience always ready to support. I took the Prince 2 Project Management course and although difficult to grasp the new terminology, I was able to pass my exams. One criticism I do have (which can be considered major perhaps) is I wish there were more practice papers for the exam. I found the current papers you do receive at the end of the course to be very different to the exams and therefore I personally struggled so much. I had to pay for external practice papers and coaching which I wish I didn't have to do. On the other hand the job searching facilities are helpful and Career Services do help improve your cover letter, CV and revamp your LinkedIn profile. I think out of all of it, this was the one I found the most beneficial. My coach was Robyn and she was very supportive and encouraging can't rate her highly enough. I haven't landed my dream Project Management job yet, but I think it's mainly due to the current job market and maybe because I'm only looking work remotely and in a rather niche industry. But I do believe that when I am ready to look again, Robyn and the team at Career Services will offer the help and support I need.

records.title: Good if you are just looking for qualifications and nothing else
records.text: The course material itself was really great and I’ve achieved my qualifications which is ultimately what I paid and set out to do. I found one particular member of the team really helpful and quick to reply - her name was Jessica, thank you Jessica! The rest of the team not so much unfortunately.When I first signed up to the course I was told I would have someone help me rewrite my CV/look at jobs etc but apart from the mention at the start no one contacted me about this at all throughout the duration of the whole year. I’m sure there was also meant to be some sort of benefits such as student discount? Again this wasn’t mentioned. While I could’ve reached out about these things myself if they were a priority for me (they weren’t luckily), given the cost of the course I think the team could have been more forthcoming with information and getting in contact with me.In terms of the exam booking process, this was quite fiddly. I don’t necessarily think the Learning People were at fault for this, more so the organisations providing the certifications. I did, however, find it extremely difficult to contact the Learning People to get my booking codes. The phone lines were always busy (I’d call different days and different times of the day) so I’d have to email. Usually I’d have to email twice.Overall, while I can’t fault the course material or online learning platform, I’m not sure I was able to get the most out of what was being offered. I’m sure this is partly down to me but the team were generally difficult to get hold of and didn’t reach out to me at all over the year unless prompted by an email.

records.title: Orientation Call at Learning People
records.text: The Instructor was very professional and knew the layout of the Learning platform very well. Patient and helpful with answering any questions. I would recommend their services.

records.title: there was not much followup from…
records.text: there was not much followup from learning people team for the course and lack of support

records.title: It was good
records.text: It was good. I got what I needed to get. One suggestion: the orienteer talked a lot, merely asked my view, little chance of asking question.

records.title: After 2 years of being a student with Learning people
records.text: After being a student with them for 2 years this is my honest review. AVERAGE is the way to describe it and definitely a bit pricey if services are not used. Don't get me wrong all staff members are great and really helpful that's probably why I signed up for another year thinking id take more use of their offered 'Services. However even when I wanted to make more use whenever you email STUDENTCARE they take roughly 3-4 days to reply sometimes they dont and you need to re-email, Calling is another story, they will 'almost' never pickup calls it was rare that I actually had someone answer my calls, in the start they were quite responsive but as the year went on and then the next it just got so bad, I get Covid hit and people get sick and leave but that's a company problem to get staff. The worst thing about learning people was the CAREER SERVICES, I wont mention names but whenever she called I would get the quickest 2-3 min call, she would ask me to send updated CV, cover letter what not.... and then would schedule you a whole month later just for another 2-3 minute call on her opinions, I'm still currently waiting on her reply from when I was a student there and haven't heard back in maybe 6 months said my subscription is ending soon can you please make some time to check my updated CV when I had maybe 2 months left with them, did not even get any help with interview questions etc, how could I when she was so busy....Best thing from this was probably gaining a new connection my Career consultant Robin, he really gave me the courage to tackle these papers but it's a shame this company really let him down as he's great but other sectors of this company need to keep up.Its hard for me to recommend Learning people to anyone as the first year to the second was a drastic decrease in service. Regardless great people willing to help besides the career service.

records.title: Customer service contacted me
records.text: Update:I was contacted by the customer service team and my program was reviewed to give me the necessary break and payment adjusted accordingly. The worst learning experience I have ever had online. They push aggressive sales over the phone, and after direct debits have been successfully set up, that is about all you will receive from them; if you ever need anything from them, they push you from one unit to the next, and most of their employees are unpleasant!I am disappointed with the lack of community support they promised while bombarding me with the sales promo, I had to watch the videos with no method of conversing, discussing, or asking questions, and their mock exams are nothing like the actual exams. Registering for the first stage of the exam was another drama, the lady that attended to my call from the exam’s unit told me it was not her work to register me for the exam. I realised I needed more than their non-interactive platform to pass the exam after the first fail, I needed time off and asked for a break and they essentially told me to keep paying the monthly charges that they don’t give break and that when the duration of the course ended, I should ask for an extension. Matthew their finance officer (as he introduced himself to me on phone) called me because they could not access the direct debit at some point, he told me that even if I am famine (famine, his exact word), I must pay that he cannot listen to me I should call learning people and bluntly told me he was just interested in collecting the fees and nothing more. I have been paid £1405 over 8 months and I wanted out please, I have lost all interest in the course and wanted to stop Matthew told me I can not opt out and the finance unit has constantly been disturbing me for fees..

records.title: For the money you pay is a bit too…
records.text: For the money you pay is a bit too less. No mentor ever answered my. So just wandered if is worht it. Not much help from anyone there.

records.title: More like a con to me.
records.text: I would have given a 1-star but decided to be generous. Also, I would have written a feedback a long time ago but decided to wait and see how things unfolds before writing.It's over a year with the Learning People and I still remember the call I had with the 'agent' (a staff of learning people) who 'deceived' me into doing my certifications with them and I specifically told him of what I needed and he talked about how it's guaranteed that I get a job through them after the courses. Now I am stuck with paying almost £3k (splited in months) and the career advisor directly told me that they don't help their students get a job, which is completely opposite of what I was told when enrolling.If this is the case, then why should I have paid such outrageous amount, I would have just register the course by myself and get the Certifications. I wouldn't want to call any other learning institution but I remembered calling one and the call advisor was so sincere to tell me that they don't help their students get a job. The reverse is the case here.Now I am stuck with about 10months of £116.46 being debited from my account and I am deeply pained whenever it leaves my account.The career session is all about bombarding one with materials to study and implement and keep networking, I think this are things seen everywhere. I expected better and was an advocate while I was started but now, I am faced with reality and sincerely can't recommend anyone here.I think the major problem is the insincerity of the first call, else their service was top notch.I am completely unhappy as none of my expectations were met, it's 14months now and about 3 months since I passed my first exam.

records.title: Avoid learning people
records.text: At the time I signed up with Learning People, I was eager to get into coding—something I had wanted to do for years. My ultimate goal was to land a job in the coding field. I was aware that I had just 12 months to complete the course, so I started off strong and made good progress.However, midway through the course, I began encountering one roadblock after another—coding is challenging, after all. But I kept pushing forward. Unfortunately, at around 75% completion, I suffered a back injury at work that left me unable to do anything for two months. Sitting down at a desk was especially difficult. Once I recovered, I resumed the course and requested an extension due to the time I had lost. They assured me that when my 12-month period was up, I should get in touch, and they would arrange something.From 86% completion to the end, I admittedly just rushed through the material without fully learning it. I didn’t want to risk being let down or forced to pay more money. As a result, I managed to complete the course within the 12-month timeframe.I paid £3,500 for the front-end developer course through Learning People. They provided me access to Codecademy’s Front-End Engineer course, which I later discovered I could have accessed directly for only about £50 per month. Looking back, I feel scammed and extremely let down by Learning People.Another big issue was the promise of mentorship. They claimed they would assign me a mentor to guide me through the course and provide additional support. I did reach out to my mentor at one point, but it was disappointing—essentially just a voice on the other end telling me to keep going and not give up. Honestly, my family could have given me the same level of encouragement for free. It’s hard to justify paying nearly £3,000 for such superficial mentorship.What’s even more frustrating is that, after completing the course, the company has never followed up with me—not once. They’ve made no effort to check on my progress, ask if I needed help, or provide any guidance on job searches in the coding field.Now, I’m in my third year of learning to code. Despite the setbacks, I’m still committed to my journey. But knowing what I know now, I would strongly advise anyone considering Learning People to save their money. If you want to learn coding, go directly to platforms like Codecademy or other reputable resources. Don’t waste your hard-earned money on Learning People.

records.title: Ghosted
records.text: Program started off promising. Was a bit pushy to get you to sign on to the program. I finished my studies and was to get some CV/job market assistance. I got a few emails from one of their reps last year and its been almost a year now since I completed my course and its been crickets. These online schools are more or less the same. They get you in, take your money and don't care how you progress or assist when complete. Definitely disappointed as they do not care about student welfare and helping you in any form to secure employment after. I understand that most of the work has to come from me and I welcome that, however not once have they done a wellness check or any feedback to see if they can assist in any way (my last interaction with them was 10/2023). They got their money, so that was all that mattered.

records.title: Prince 2 project management course is…
records.text: Prince 2 project management course is not very well structured at all. I failed my exam 2 times, then decided to move course provider (actually made me doubt myself hugely which is the worst part). Passed exam in two weeks with a huge pass percentage with new provider. Course has many typos, the segments do not even tell what flaming chapter to look at in the manual while studying, half the time I get to the end of a small segment and say to myself 'learnt absolutely nothing there' or I spend more time filtering through the manual to find out whats what. Terrible platform, trying to get through Agile course at the moment with these guys, but close to moving to the other provider.Edit for response: To clarify, I passed the foundation exam first time as is the basics of the method, its quite simple to understand and unfortunately a lot came from watching you tube videos. Practitioner (which is putting the method into practice) is more difficult to some.It’s says a lot that this reply is to try and discredit my review and integrity. I was complaining about the course you provide, not your support service. Why you felt the need to bring this to attention can only be viewed as suspect.You say you have an 80% pass rate but in what context? If you actually evaluate that statistic on the assumption that students did not have to pay any more money either in resits or time extensions I think that statistic would be drastically lower. The check in phone calls were basically a courtesy call, no support or advice were given, all I received were patronising tones. I have only been offered to move over to a different platform because I made this review. Moving to this next platform I will see if it is any better, but it clarifies that you understand the product you are selling is inadequate for the students, in turn if you still offer that platform, you know it is at fault and students will find it harder to get through, meaning more resits to pay and time extensions to pay.Unfortunately this reply came too early, should have waited until I was on the next platform as I may have well removed this review as I may have felt differently. You should use bad reviews as a tool to make your service better, not use the discrediting tactic to spin the review on your client, all it’s does is frustrate your client further. Simple business intelligence.

records.title: Got what I asked for but do feel it wasn't great value for money.
records.text: I signed up to the course as I wanted a change in career and through fault of my own, this changed shortly after beginning. I cannot argue too much as I signed up and agreed the price and payment. In hindsight however, I do feel that for what was offered (despite me not completing it) that it was fairly overpriced and not really great value for money. I did carry out some of the modules whilst I was still mentally invested and found it to be quite old fashioned revision videos. I am still paying off the full amount which I will owe for until the end of 2025 which I will be glad to see the back of. In hindsight, I feel I would have found the price of the exams online and set my own revision plan up as I can guarantee that it would not come up to the ££££'s that it costs instead of buying an 'exam package' from a third part company. Either way, lesson learnt.

records.title: Took the programming course

records.title: Student Loan Cancelled - Avoid
records.text: I completed an undergrad with Arden University several years ago when they were RDI. The course material was from Anglia Ruskin and though it was basic, it wasn't bad. The tutors were hit and miss, some really good, others not so good. But being able to study the course I wanted as a distance learner (I had to work and couldn't study in person) made university accessible for me and I'm grateful to have graduated with a 2:1. I returned to the university in October to start a Postgraduate course. My student advisor was helpful though a little pushy to take my deposit - I had wanted to wait until my student loan was approved. She knew it was approved before I did - long before the confirmation letter from SFE - and again pushed for the deposit. I paid. I got access to iLearn, and completed the Milestones required as part of their induction program. You need to do this for your student loan to be confirmed. Then I found out that Arden cancelled my student loan the day before my course start date, incorrectly telling SFE that I hadn't attended. I contacted Student Support for help, and three days went by before they responded that I should contact their Student Finance instead. It takes 22 days for the change to be actioned with SFE so I was pushing for a quick resolution but there was no urgency on Arden's part. That the Student Support didn't refer my ticket to Student Finance was irritating, there was no proactivity or any real help from them. I then read some reviews of Arden and saw several stating the same experience as me. I didn't want to wrestle with Arden for months as other students were doing, so I withdrew. I withdrew on November 6th, completing their withdrawal form and requesting a refund. I received the formal withdrawal completion on December 2nd. I have followed up several times for the refund, it's now December 23rd and there is no sign of it. I raised a new ticket with the Refunds team on December 5th, received their auto-response but have had no movement from them at all. Their own timeframes dictate they will respond within 5 working days, it's now been 11 days since my latest ticket, no response to any of them.   I have called Arden Student Finance four times. Once I was on hold for an hour before giving up. The other three times I managed to get through to someone, they said I needed to speak to someone else and that someone else would call me back "right away". The last time was two weeks ago. No one calls back. I will continue to hound them for this refund because of the principle. Other information: Applying was easy, the application process is straightforward and the advisor was helpful and quick to respond to get through the process swiftly.Their iLearn platform looks good, but when you get into it, it's very busy with a lot of information and not much of it useful. It's dated and though they close the platform for two weeks between periods for "maintenance" the material still has a lot of broken links, out of date content, and old meeting recordings which aren't useful anymore. The Induction Module is somewhat useful and it's mandatory for you to complete it along with the accompanying assessment. It's straightforward and simple. But you also have to attend a mandatory induction webinar, which is two hours long and they are just going over this induction module. There's no additional useful information and at 2 hours, it's not realistic for neuro-diverse students and is largely a waste of everyone's time.

records.title: Unskilled tutors and poorly written lessons
records.text: I am on the BSc psychology distance learning program and I agree with the other reviewers who highlighted awesome tutors such as Ant and Holly. But the majority of the tutors aren’t very competent. They are not experts on the module subjects, not articulate/good at teaching, and just doing the bare minimum. Many are phd students. Furthermore, a lot of the lessons are poorly written. It’s usually just copy-pasting from the textbook, plus some videos from unreliable sources (like random YouTube creators) or Ted talks. Mistakes are commonly spotted. If you only have time and resource for distance learning, and you are self-driven enough, Arden is a decent choice. You can read textbooks yourself and build a good foundation in psychology. Just don’t expect too much from the uni.

records.title: Find another place to study.
records.text: Decent tutors are few and far between.  Access to academic journals are limited, with lecturers recommending Google Scholar rather than any library Arden provides.  Student support are poor, often rude, patronising and down right irritating. No communication is ever proactive, I have to chase them for a link to enrol and pay for every module and I have contacted student support several times in the last week, to be told only today that 'there is a technical issue and they should be with me by the end of the week' on the final day my results should be sent. records.title: Aggressive sales, decent course, but somewhat lacking
records.text: I took Lean Six Sigma Black Belt through the Knowledge Academy. They were very aggressive when I initially inquired about the course, and continued to call repeatedly even after I asked that they only contact me via email. They then took forever on the phone before they would give me a price, and only then would they email the quote to me, placing a very short deadline on it. That said, once I purchased the course, customer service was very responsive and helped me with issues encountered during the course. The course itself was easy to follow, with his materials, although the instructor basically just read the slides. Several of the quizzes covered material that had not yet been introduced in the course. The key issue was with the required software program. The only way to access it was through a few trial which expired well before I finished the course. The only solution Knowedge Academy provided was to sign up for more free trials with different email addresses. I have since learned that most similar programs offer free 1 year licenses for this program. I am ultimately satisfied with what I learned, but I would choose a different certification company next time.

records.title: Aimed at exam goers, not learners
records.text: The course seemed to be aimed at exam goers rather than to those who wanted to learn the subject at a high level. Overall an OK course but I wouldn't do any more of these as they appear to be aimed at adding a tick box on a CV.Trainer was ok but needs to be more focused on giving the definition of concepts before talking through examples.

records.title: Trainer lacks examples of real situations
records.text: I requested the trainer to be based in UK and English spoken when I originally booked this course so was disappointed that the trainer was from India so lacked the communication skills you require to run these courses.  In addition, the trainer lacked examples of real situations and seems not enough experience in the field. Trainer presents in a prescriptive way.I also faced issues when login to my course via zoom which was the same issue I faced in my course earlier in the year with Knowledge Academy.  I highlighted this to KA and preempted this by discussing this before the course commenced, but yet the same issue was faced; and I was unable to contact customer service easily on the day as this course was held on the weekend.

records.title: A very straightforward set of materials, delivered in an unengaging way
records.text: This Knowledge Academy course was geared well towards the certification it was set up for. The course content, which was provided in advance is tailored perfectly to the exam syllabus with an appropriate but manageable amount of detail. However, little thought seems to have been given to the design of the course's delivery, which consisted mainly of the instructor talking through the slides which had been provided in advance with minimal engagement. Whilst there are obviously challenges with digital learning, it was uninspiring to see so little variation in the teaching style especially given that best practice learning design was part of the content for this course! From a logistical POV, more details could have been clearly communicated ahead of time about how and when to book online exams - and what the structure of teaching days would look like - given the cost of the course and the time commitment required it was disappointing for sessions to end early, with little else to do than look at sample exam papers - which had already been provided.Overall this experience was not great, and felt like it had been prepared to meet the bare minimum requirements of preparing candidates for the APMG certification exam.

records.title: Excellent smooth experience
records.text: This is a balanced review of studying the Proofreading Diploma course with NCC Home Learning. I signed up to do the Proofreading course a few months ago, and purchased the course online via their website. The price NCC were offering was cheaper than another alternative I was looking at, making them an easy choice to do this course with. Sign up was easy. Once I'd paid, I was given a login and the course wad added to my login within 24 hours, and I was ready to go.The onboarding portal to the course is easy to navigate with clear direction. The course material was easy to download, and it was easy to upload my assignments with it too. The course itself was good. The materials were easy to read and included lots of good examples to demonstrate the teachings. There were 7 units which were good, though I felt the course felt too short and simplistic, as there were elements of proofreading that weren't really covered. I think a couple of extra units would have made the course a bit more comprehensive and better value. The marking/feedback experience was good. My units were all marked swiftly, pretty much all within a week. I passed each unit first time so I didn't require any feedback in terms of correction, so I can't comment on this, but I was very pleased with the efficient and speedy marking process. On completion of the course, I was told to email NCC to apply for my certificate. Their response was prompt and I received my certificate in about a month, and I was fully informed through the process while I was waiting for it. When I signed up to the course, I got an invite to sign up to a student discount subscription service. I didn't use this as the discounts offered didn't appeal to me, but it might appeal to others as it offered a mix of discounts on eating, fashion, entertainment etc. Overall, very pleased with NCC. Pros:- Cheaper than alternatives for this course- Quick and easy sign up- Minimalist, easy to use website/learning portal- Enjoyable course, easy to understand with good assignment exercises- Efficient marking- Good communication from NCC- Received my certificate quickly- Discounted courses for returning customers- Student discount invite (for those that it appeals to) Cons: - Course was a bit short for my taste, could have been more comprehensive/detailed.

records.title: Disappointing change in awarding body
records.text: I choose NCC Home Learning as they provided a level 3 diploma in Business Administration accredited by NCFE. I enjoyed the course and found the tutor feedback extremely helpful. Customer service was excellent and by the end of the course I was already planning which course i'd do next. Then my certificate arrived. I cannot even express how disappointed I was. I didn't get my NCFE accredited diploma. I got a certificate of achievement from ABC Awards. Both the name and certificate looked highly unprofessional. I emailed NCC Home Learning immediately to ask why I received an ABC Certificate of achievement and not a diploma certificate accredited by NCFE. The only reason I signed up for the course was because it was NCFE. I was told the awarding body had now changed to ABC. I asked if I could return the ABC cert and get a NCFE cert. I was told I could. At the time I was working abroad so as soon as I returned to England I emailed again to apologise for the delay and I would return the certificate today for my replacement. I was then told NCFE would no longer offer the diploma certificate. So after months of hard work completing the course and expecting to achieve a diploma certificate I have ended up with a certificate of achievement that looks so unprofessional I'm embarrassed to show it to potential employers.  Waste of my time and money. I'm so disappointed.  I originally signed up for NCFE I should have been awarded NCFE especially as I had already completed 50% of the course when the awarding body changed.

records.title: Worst experience
records.text: Forensic Psychology level 3.I have the last module to complete, submitted last assignment 47 days ago and no reply.Had to chase every single time the graded work (except for the first two). Thankfully I did not need much support from my tutor, as the only time I emailed a question it took 3 weeks for her to reply. I have been unwell for some time and have also difficulty typing, so I purchased voice software to help me. But it is ridicolous, no support from tutor beside grading (whenever she was available which was rare), no feedback beside the work submitted, no reply, no updates, I chased the fact that I was over the planned time because it was taking too long. Voila' a reply was received and graded paper followed. However I was told that if I wanted to extend I had to pay £60. What? Beside the fact that the T&C's do mention if the student wanted to extend there could be a charge arranged, so nowhere is the mention of a fixed fee, and besides, the supposed 10 working days turnaround time was hardly ever adhered. So where did the figure come from...Anyway, I am now stuck with no reply, no graded last module and, possibly, not being able to complete the course and get certification unless I pay more. Which I won't do. You live and you learn, but I'd say if you decide to go for a course with them, make sure to get everything clear from the start.I am only giving it 2 stars rather than 1 as I enjoyed the course modules.I am also very suspicious about hardly any reviews under 5 stars or so, as mentioned by someone in a previous review which was of a negative experience.

records.title: Avoid NCC courses by Study House
records.text: It's a real shame as I am not one to leave negative reviews, but my current experience leaves me little choice but to offer caution to others. NCC undoubtedly has great reviews, and I don't doubt the high quality or the varsity of these reviews. HOWEVER, my daughter took out a business planning course with NCC, which NCC told us was delivered by a partner organisation called Study House. We received the study materials which consisted entirely of just PDFs of reading material. No video content, not checkpoints, no quizzes or other interactive elements. Just written material literally from a book. Worst course content presentation I've ever seen (and I've worked as a lecturer for 10 years). We agreed that this wasn't what she wanted to spend over £400 for and asked for a refund. We were told to contact Study House, which I declined, since we paid NCC, and therefore should receive a refund from such. It's now been over 3 weeks, and we keep being told that information will be checked with managers, but no progress whatsoever. Communication stopped 10 days ago and yet they dared taking it another payment for a course we don't want. Very frustrating! My advice, NCC is bad at running partnerships, and: avoid Study House courses offered by NCC.

records.title: Misleading marketing
records.text: I applied for a tutoring job advertised by NCC. The advert stated that if you don't have the necessary qualifications then don't worry you can study on the NCC's courses and then become a tutor with them. The advert clearly implied, however, that there were current jobs available for which already qualified candidates would be considered. It was on this basis that I made my application. NCC proceeded to tell me that I am not qualified but recommended that I spend around one thousand pounds and a lot of study time gaining a list of qualifications provided by NCC. I was disappointed and am concerned that an educational establishment would recommend to a prospective student that they spend time and money studying for qualifications that they already have the equivalent of. I contacted them about this and they said I could reapply but stated that there aren't actually any current positions in the subject area for which I applied and for which they had advertised. This is really misleading marketing.** Edited in order to respond to NCC's reply below **- I'm happy to acknowledge that I haven't studied on any of the courses at NCC and therefore my comments do not pertain to the quality of the content or delivery of the courses. I rewrote the review after not being able to find the other one on the site (my mistake). - Point taken about the assessors qualification, but that leaves two other qualifications recommended that I already had the equivalent of. - Advertising jobs that don't actually exist at the time of the advert. Not misleading marketing?

records.title: The course trainer (Pawel) was engaging and it was a pleasant environment to learn in however the content needs improvement.
records.text: The course trainer ‘Pawel’ was engaging and a generally nice person with lots of experience which made this an enjoyable course. I personally believe that most of the content is great however some of the content needs improvement specifically around statements, handcuffing and ABD. The course teaches people to use handcuffs, this is a use of force that should be clearly justified and this (in my opinion) should be followed by the law aspect of the course - so you can properly learn to justify actions to prevent criminal action. Police have 5 reasons to use handcuffs and they have to justify this - so should SIA licensed operatives to protect integrity and to ‘cover’ their actions.  The statements part of the course is informative however you are expected to write a statement which is liable in court but the course doesn’t really offer enough detail on what should be expected for a statement in court and can leave those without experience vulnerable. ABD - There is 1 specific slide that covers the  awareness of  ABD which is fine but it doesn’t really emphasise the importance of calling 999 immediately if some is suspected to be in ABD crisis. I believe that there should also be more detail on how someone presents with ABD and the risks  associated. In general, the course is good. It is up to date with the latest laws and threats to the country and work places.

records.title: Great Experience, But Unhelpful Advice :(
records.text: I really enjoyed the beginning where the Dr briefly covered the anatomy, and relevant biology we needed to know. I think he explained the pain assessment model SOCRATES and the other strands of taking medical histories pretty well as he gave example questions for each stage. The opportunity to take histories was great - I wish more of us would have had the chance to try it, so perhaps a follow-up session to practice taking histories in order to develop communication would be possible in the near future? I think the Dr had useful advice during the Q&A, but I did not appreciate the subtle, but present tone of disapproval when students raised questions about the UCAT. It is one thing to encourage students to get organised and ahead of the curve, but telling them they are ‘so far behind’, and that their peers had started months ago is not useful nor kind. The UCAT registration is in 3 months, which is more than enough time, and encouraging an unhealthily competitive culture so early on will only be detrimental later when students are in medical school. Overall, great experience for taking histories, but I wish the Dr was more authentic and empathetic in his advice (it felt as though he was trying to sell us the MedicHut packages by making us feel like we were at the back of the pack - which is not accurate!)

records.title: UCAT review

records.title: I wouldn't recommend this crash course
records.text: I wouldn't recommend this crash course. The content is packed into short sessions with minimal breaks, which makes it overwhelming and hard to absorb. It's also not interactive enough, leaving you feeling lost at times. As a widening participation student, I expected more value for money, but unfortunately, it fell short of expectations. After the two days, there was no follow-up support, which felt very disconnected. A WhatsApp group or some way to continue asking questions and interacting with tutors would have been really helpful. Overall, I feel it was a waste of both money and time.

records.title: Bad Customer Support, Good Interviewers
records.text: My sole reason for the lowly rated review is that the customer support I spoke with said the masterclass would be for Panel & MMI Interviews, however after attending it I realized that it was more closely designed to MMI interviews only with the second day consisting of an MMI mock, leaving Panel interviews completely neglected.The interviewers were professional and provided good feedback, and the lessons were interactive. The only downside is customer support lying to me, as I'm still trying to figure out what this has to do with panel interviews, in the 1st day as well, aspects of interviews were described that related more closely towards MMI interviews.Overall, if you're sitting an MMI interview, 100%, go for it. If not, I wouldn't suggest it, and don't listen to customer support.Regards.

records.title: Lean six sigma course
records.text: I made a request to complete the yellow belt and green belt six sigma course. It was sold to me, where I agreed to use e careers on a finance option as had to fund it myself but later found I was mis-sold.I was told they offer Exam Pass Guarantee and it was explained to me that it means I can keep doing the exam at no additional cost until I pass the exam. I completed the course. The instructor is knowledgeable at his subject and can’t fault, he was supportive as best as you being a virtual course. Only feedback is missing slides should be added into the course notes. I passed my yellow belt exam and then went to complete my green belt exam which I failed. I request to resit which a new voucher was sent and again did next exam and failed. Both were very close to passing and I feel there was questions on the exam that was taught, which 8 think the exam should be looked at to make sure all material is available. When I spoke to E career they then informed me it would be at a cost. I explained how it was sold and even asked to listen to my recording when sold (which they couldn’t as recordings only kept for 6 months). I got a little bit of discount from £300 to £275 but they offered me a free resit to if I failed third time, so fourth was free but was told I need to recomplete the 3 day course again.  I also asked about the finance which they advertise as 0% interest and I’m paying interest (so they should update their website that interest is paid) but basically told nothing they can do. So in summary be careful on the Exam Pass Guarantee if sold as it’s not guarantee pass unless willing to pay £300. Also interest rate is not 0% and if it is I wasn’t offered this. Also they don’t do any mock exam during the course as advertised on day 4 but one is emailed to go through yourself.

records.title: Get the books and self-study!
records.text: I completed my business analysis diploma from April 2023 to May 2024 with some delay due to a death in the family a third through, I was unable to complete it within the 7-8 months I hoped but did a good job on my own! I would advise anyone wishing to take a course with e-careers to first decide whether you are a good home/ online learner or need guided materials. The reason being is that the materials provided when I studied with them were quite out of date and so by the 2nd module I asked for a refund. What got me was that if I didn’t already have some of the profession recommended bought books and was going through them at the same time, I would never had known and this could have cost me dearly in exam fees. When I contacted e-careers, I was told the course was being updated however, I didn’t receive materials for the modules I had already taken. I was upset and left a review at that time which I was asked to take down and was offered money back plus for them to only issue the exam vouchers already paid for. I accepted the offer. Hence, I self- studied the entire course and didn’t use the materials as it was too vague and out of date. I worked hard and purchased all the books recommended on the syllabus for each module by BCS who were helpful and it was all quite simple with them. I wish I had started the journey with BCS in the beginning. Note that if you want a good understanding of business analysis and if you’re not already working as one, do not feel rushed to complete this course quickly. By me thoroughly reading the books and making my own notes it really helped my understanding and grew my confidence. Also, as I received no after care upon completion of the oral exam, where I had to call e-careers to ask what was on offer - there is a free career growth masterclass you can sign up for. My overall experience with e-careers was disappointing and I found the staff unpleasant, and a loss of communication between subject staff v sales. Anyway, my hard work paid off but please do think about your options and how thorough you want to learn and buy the books! The books is what passes you not the poorly designed slides or e-textbook from the course provider.
