records.title: Bootcamp experience
records.text: 1. The course material is outdated.2.When a question is asked on the Discord no one from HyperionDev gets back to you, only fellow students.3. Different reviewers have different opinions on what the task requirements are.The support team was helpful and I liked the feedback from the reviewers.

records.title: Very basic but has potential!
records.text: Very basic but has potential!A very concise and thrilling way to learn!The company provides you with many resources, from live lectures that you can watch back at a later stage, to logical PDFs containing a nice breakdown of each topic. Although I find the PDFs and lectures don't always cover the knowledge needed for tasks. Extra reading up online will be needed!The support via 1-1 mentor calls, is a lovely touch as it is very personalised and gives you more confidence when unsure of something. I do feel the mentors are also limited in knowledge, as once he was struggling to find the problem.The dashboard is very user friendly and easy to navigate. The links are helpful to go to dropbox, lecture schedules and submit/view our task deadlines.The only downside I would say is that the particular course I am on was quite fast paced for my lifestyle with children, I wish they would be able to extend it to a part time position rather than full time.

records.title: Good Teaching, Not So Good Organisation
records.text: The quality of the teaching itself is very good, with clearly defined modules and excellent explanations of how to program through live lectures and short pre-recorded lectures.The mentor calls were a nightmare to book, with some only being available seven days later. Ae the mentor calls are essential to fully grasp some of the concepts, I fell behind. I was enrolled as a late starter and additional help was offered, though I didn't really see this. Because of a glitch, I was under the false impression that I was on target with tasks, only to find I was behind once HyperionDev had resolved the glitch, which further dented my motivation. They then changed the course halfway through to make around half the modules optional. The communications are all auto-based, so it feels like you are dealing with robots, and comes across as very impersonal.I'd only recommend this course if you can take it on a full-time basis, as I found the workload was immense and was too tricky to fit around working a full-time job.

records.title: The bootcamp is great for beginners but…
records.text: The bootcamp is great for beginners but the biggest flaw is how this is organised:-Timetable not clear-Never sure what topics will be covered in each week-My cohort seems to be mixed with others so I see the same lectures twice... very confusing

records.title: The grading of assignments is a bit…
records.text: The grading of assignments is a bit slow, submitted some assignments for 10 days and not get graded, therefore have no idea if I am doing well.The instructors are very nice, helpful and informative.

records.title: Good introductory data science bootcamp
records.text: I learned a lot in the DfE-funded data science bootcamp. In 3 months, I've come from not being able to code at all, to now developing simple data solutions for the company I'm working for. The basic Python modules were good & covers a wide range of topics. The mentors were really friendly and helpful. I appreciate the mentors' patience and perseverance to help us during particularly challenging modules.Looking back at the bootcamp once I've finished it, I have some suggestions: the basic Python techniques in the 1st half could be better integrated with the data science modules in the 2nd half. As it was, the two halves seem like separate courses. In other words, since we only had 12-16 weeks, perhaps the Python-for-Python's-sake modules can be reduced, or packaged better for data science and machine learning in Jupyter noteboooks (for example: combining 2D lists with discussions on NumPy, building custom functions to clean data, or OOP to build a non-standard scaler). Also, if possible, try to use business cases in your examples (instead of the commonly used iris datasets) to better prepare graduates for a new job in a new industry.Thanks very much! Keep up the good work!

records.title: The software engineering course was…
records.text: The software engineering course was very informative and educational.It'll be great even for the people that are new in the development industry, the course helps you create application that can be added into your professional profile. Marking  response time could be improved though.

records.title: Software engineering bootcamp
records.text: The software engineering bootcamp is good and the support I received from mentors or the support team in general was amazing, they’re knowledgeable and helpful. Areas of improvement:• Content can be hard to understand, especially for beginners with no coding background. I had a small amount of coding knowledge and still struggled here and there. • In certain tasks, explanations were not concise. Sometimes I found that information was irrelevant, making the documents unnecessarily long. • Sometimes mentors were highly unprofessional, I have had a session where the connection was bad and they just continued with the work. And another session that the mentor failed to communicate that they could not make it to the meeting, TWICE. Overall, the bootcamp was good, the support team and mentors are great at what they do. Sometimes it can be frustrating for the reasons I mentioned above.

records.title: The lecture slides don’t cover…

records.title: Hyperion dev experience
records.text: Great institution if your looking at a career change or to get a understanding of software development. It’s always best to do an in person course as that way you recieve guidance by the mentors and your program goes quicker The pros of this institution, I landed a software development job within the same year (Note they don’t job hunt for you), the work is well documented, variety of like minded individuals.Cons, the institution is very straight forwards meaning don’t expect something extraordinary if you are looking for a university setup then rather apply at one, the course is marketed as a 3 month in person but takes atleast 5-6 months as there’s 3 sections and each section has about 30 lessons and some lessons like capstones can take up to a week so don’t expect to be done within 3 monthsOverall I done what I needed to do to get the job I wanted. If you think it’s something you are interested in and fully invested then I’ll definitely recommend giving it a shot definitely not a program you want to do half heartedly

records.title: I did the initial application tasks and…
records.text: I did the initial application tasks and completed the application for the software Engineer DfE bootcamp.I struggled through the tasks to complete them as the examples given did not cover half of what the questions asked.However, today I got offered a place, not on the Software Engineering bootcamp, but they want to put me on the Data Science bootcamp instead.No thanks, that is not what I applied for.After reading the reviews here, it looks like I have dodged a bullet and saved a huge amount of time and effort.

records.title: A total disappointment!
records.text: My course finishes tomorrow and I am totally disappointed. Lessons are PDF notes on dropbox. One could get used to it if it were not for the fact that the lessons do not contain the information necessary to solve the tasks! This is terribly frustrating. You have to search on the internet for hours and then you end up on some website where someone asks for the answer and it is the only option for you because you do not even know exactly how to search because you are new to coding. For personal reasons, it has been really difficult for me because in the meantime things have come up that have really limited my free time. And every time I sat down to do an assignment, it turned out that I actually had to spend 3h/4h to find the answers on the internet. God! I thought maybe I was just too stupid but it turns out a lot of people have the same problem as I can see from the reviews.When I applied for the course there were no negative reviews! Now there are lots, how can this be?

records.title: Not organised
records.text: Not organised, not good structures and topics where random to just finish the funded bootcamp

records.title: Find another course provider
records.text: The bootcamp was good in a sense as I am now trying to become a software engineer. There were however many things which let the course down:The lecture hours were really helpful and our lecturer Logan was fantastic. There just wasn't enough lectures and there was a lot left out.A lot of this course was self learning and doing via outdated PDFs which must have been made 5+years ago because a lot of the information was outdated. Also, the briefs were often misleading and vague meaning that deciphering them were more difficult than the tasks.The career support service was non-existent. The companies used to give talks, guidance and promote their vacancies were irrelevant and often required university graduates only which is not the level most of the students were at.The community servers were also removed because students began asking the staff why certain failing procedures were in place. The owner Riaz also took every complaint personally and lashed out on these servers. He made the overall experience worse. He directly emailed students who had anonymously complained and harassed them for information. They also kicked several students off of the course.My fellow students were the best part of this experience where we have now developed a community (the right way) and help each other with coding queries, emotional support and job hunting.It seemed apparent towards the end of the course that the main focus was not the success or wellbeing of the students, but more how many milestones they could push us through as quickly as possible to be paid their next installment from the government.My advice for those looking to join a bootcamp: find another company, there are loads out there.

records.title: Online Full Stack Web Dev Course Dec 2022-June 23
records.text: Recently graduated from the Online Full Stack Web Development course. After completing the course, I feel that I've learned an incredible amount and am fluent in HTML, Javascript, and CSS as well as React.Overall, there were a few problems with the course. The way that it works is you have access to folders containing PDFs which you read and complete tasks, for which you need to do additional research which is fine. There are also some video lectures, which are helpful during the first section (basics) but as you progress through the course there are fewer of them and they become less useful / out of date. I found that the course PDFs were often out of date and missing key steps for how to create the apps that they required to pass the course. All they need to do is update the course materials, which is what we pay for. This caused a lot of stress and is unacceptable for a course for which you pay thousands of UK £'s. One word of warning is that the time frame they give you for earlier tasks are very reasonable, but towards the end they become near impossible. The final suggested time frame occurs after the end of support, which is concerning. This seriously needs reviewing because from the discord forum it looks like this happened to a few people, and they had to pay to have their support extended. Hyperion need to review this. My advice is get two weeks ahead of this timeline before you get into the last month - you'll need it.I did have calls with Mentors on a couple of occasions and they were useful in talking you through how to complete tasks. One mentor even took my task away and sent it back to me a day later with suggestions which was very helpful.On two occasions I requested help through the ticketing system (once because the course materials mentioned additional reading which hadn't been provided, and once because one of my tasks was reviewed incorrectly) and received no help at all. I just gave up asking for help via the ticketing system.I didn't do the course with University accreditation but I would be interested to hear if the level of support was better if you did the University accredited version of the course.

records.title: Terrible Administration and Structure
records.text: I have just "Completed" the bootcamp with Hyperion Dev.First of all the whole structure and admin of this bootcamp is incredibly poor. They are in need of someone who knows what they are doing to come in and take ownership of it because on my course not one person has been satisfied with the delivery, and I also read in another discord the same kind of tone.First of all, the entry tests are in Python and are HARDER than the actual 12/62 tasks that you need to do to graduate from this course..... The Python is not relevant one bit to the web development course either. On completion they emailed me saying I was in the web dev cohort then put me into the software development course, something I was not interested in. The online chat on their website is worse than a BOT, nobody ever replies, and my mate who is currently looking into this keeps telling me that nobody replies on it also. And after about 6 emails they changed me onto the web development one.  Ok I thought we had some success.... NO. The dashboard has always been the wrong dates for me, for example, it would say that my average completion time for a task would be 10th of January, however the lecture for that task would be the 15th of January. Which annoyed me as that's no way to track progress and it always said I was behind, and I would get auto generated emails saying this also.I would also constantly get invitations for a previous cohort lectures, it took 6 emails to finally get this changed.On top of this the lectures which I thought would be between 9-5 originally ended up being 4pm every day, which sometimes go on to 6 or 7pm. I have commitments outside of the working hours so this just made a lot of lectures hard to go to. However, you can view them as they are recorded.I know a lot of the other students have not had a good experience, and I have up to this point stuck up for Hyperion Dev, however the final straw for me was...I was ill for two weeks and having tests in hospo, in that time nobody checked up. So it got to Monday and I got up early and thought I would now crack on and catch up, when I started getting emails from HD congratulating me on completing the bootcamp. My dashboard now says that I'm 100% completed of the mandatory tasks (the first 12), and all other tasks are optional. For someone who originally signed up for structured learning this is not good. Now I just have no motivation to finish and it just comes across as a joke. So basically as long as you complete the first 12 tasks that are a lot easier than the entry tasks then you pass. ASLONG as you apply for jobs in this time. This is because they are now pushing everyone to get a job because I guess it hits their target so they get a bonus. It feels his way anyway. And the most stupid thing is they are offering a certification from a Uni...... AFTER you get a job offer. By the time I get a job I'm not going to need a certification because I already have a job. Anyway, the whole thing is a joke, and I would have rather have not done it now. I had given up work to do this process and it's just been a complete job. The study material in my opinion wasn't bad, and the lecturer Pieter was good. It is just the whole structure / admin / let's get keep people out of the door attitude that has ruined it. Hyperion Dev does need someone to come in and sort out their communications, emails, structure of delivery etc.... Hope this review helps.*** Addition - My friend who got accepted, received today 4/3/2023, an email stating that orientation will be between 25th - 31st October 2022 ....... -_-***** Just to add, the replies from them are so robotic and unhelpful. I guarantee they respond to this comment with a generic template saying that I am anonymous. My name is in the review.

records.title: Outstanding Support from SHEilds and Leah Frayne
records.text: As a Senior Logistics Manager, I’ve decided to take the next step in my career by enrolling in the NVQ Level 6 in Health and Safety with SHEilds. Leah was absolutely brilliant. She explained everything in clear, simple terms and took the time to help me fully understand my options. What really impressed me was her knowledge, there wasn’t a single question she couldn’t answer and her ability to guide me without any pressure. She made everything feel straightforward and manageable, turning what could have been a stressful process into a genuinely exciting one.Leah also went above and beyond when it came to discussing payment options. She carefully broke down the different choices available, making it easy for me to plan. But the confidence and trust she inspired in me, coupled with her positive and supportive approach, made me so certain in my decision that I happily chose to pay the full fee upfront. I’ve never felt so excited to start a course, and that’s entirely down to the fantastic service I’ve received.SHEilds doesn’t just offer the best rates in the industry, they deliver outstanding support every step of the way. Leah’s guidance and professionalism have been second to none, and it’s clear that SHEilds is an organisation that genuinely cares about the success of its students.I would recommend SHEilds without hesitation to anyone considering a career in health and safety. I’ve already told friends and colleagues about my great experience, and I’d encourage anyone looking for the right training provider to reach out to Leah. Her knowledge, approachability, and genuine care make all the difference.Thank you to SHEilds for such an amazing experience so far, and a special thank you to Leah for all her help, patience, and encouragement. I’m so excited to start this course, and I know I’ve made the best choice. Keep up the excellent work!

records.title: FIRST
records.text: FIRST: If the reassessment process is taking too long, this could indicate an issue with the workflow or evaluation criteria. It may be helpful to establish a clearer timeline for reassessment and set expectations for when feedback should be received. You could propose a streamlined process or ask for transparency on the factors causing delays.Second-Word Limit and Detailed Explanation: If you are required to give more detailed explanations while being restricted by a word limit, this can hinder clarity. It would be useful to request flexibility in the word count, especially when more context is needed. Alternatively, you could suggest focusing on the key points first and allowing further elaboration through follow-up questions or meetings, ensuring efficiency without sacrificing depth.

description:
Broadbent & Co was set up in 1996 by Steven and Elizabeth Broadbent. Steve was the Chair of the National Network for Access Centres until 2013 and so very much involved in DSA developments at a national level.

Their ethos was simple, the belief that "everyone must be seen and treated as an individual with their own individual needs. These needs must be identified in order for them to realise their own potential in education, employment and for life".

In May 2018, Steve very sadly passed away. His son, Andrew, continues to follow in his footsteps and is the CEO of Broadbent Assist Ltd, Director alongside Elizabeth Broadbent, and he is also an active Needs Assessor.

Their dedication to student success really shines through. I highly recommend Ideal schools.

records.title: Great experience easy to use website
records.text: Great experience easy to use website, people at the college are friendly, never scared or embarassed if stuck with something, they explain it in a way that you understand.   Would highly recommend to anyone thinking about taking a course with them

records.title: ICB Level 2 Bookkeeping
records.text: I have just completed my ICB Level 2 Bookkeeping with Ideal Schools. I couldn’t have asked for a better service.Communication great throughout, and also super helpful tutors who are a great support when you need it.Huge thanks to Scot who has supported me throughout my Level 2.

records.title: I recently passed with distinction the…
records.text: I recently passed with distinction the ICB Level 3 Diploma in Payroll Management with Ideal Schools. Many thanks to Nikki and all at Ideal Schools. As always they were helpful, approachable and made studying a pleasure.

records.title: Just completed AAT level 2 with Ideal…
records.text: Just completed AAT level 2 with Ideal schools, I have found the whole process from choosing which course provider to choose to the tutor support throughout really friendly and approachable. I am now studying payroll management and also moving on to AAT level 3 and 4. I like the fact there's really no pressure and time constraints, I work full time and also have a busy family life so although I do set days times for study time sometimes that doesn't always go to plan so it has taken me longer than probably most people to complete. ideal schools are always supportive as well as the student support group.

records.title: Really enjoyed the courses
records.text: Really enjoyed the courses, my Tutor was great and my assignments were assessed quickly with very helpful feedback on each one.My only criticism is that some of the study material and assessments had incorrect information in them and I had to highlight this to my Tutor, which was quickly resolved, but this can be a bit off putting, when you sit there trying to answer a question which has the incorrect information in and does waste time.

records.title: Great people
records.text: Excellent tutor and admin team - responsive, polite and demonstrably hardworking. Nicky is knowledgeable and keen to build a strong understanding of the content with her students. Wish study material had more questions to practice with.

records.title: Great student support
records.text: I have studied with Ideal schools for L2 (ICB) and am now on L3. The team provide excellent support on the phone and in marking assignments quickly. They are also really efficient at booking the exams so I am making good progress. I would definitely recommend them. I'm glad I chose a training provider rather than just studying from textbooks as I feel you learn a lot more from being able to ask questions. The way the courses are structured prepares you well for the real exams.

records.title: A School I'd recommend
records.text: I very successfully completed my ICB Payroll qualification after following the course with Ideal Schools. They gave me plenty of practise and came back with feedback very quickly every time, after completing the different assignments. The course syllabus could do with some reviewing/updating here and there though. (Only reason why I'm not giving the full 5 stars)

records.title: A good range of online support from…
records.text: A good range of online support from tutors, but I feel the hours could be extended to some evenings and weekends.I feel some of the content of the course could be in greater detail as when I have come to take exams or mock exams some of the questions haven't been covered. Other than that, I like the way the folders are set out with progress tests as you go along. The tutors and ideal schools team have been excellent, I can't fault them at all.

records.title: Good support
records.text: Good support, always available to answer queries where needed. Only criticism is around the course overview with regards to time. It wasn't clear what the course FULLY entailed, e.g. how many mock exams, how many real exams etc. so this made planning my time for the full course a bit tricky!

records.title: Great experience with Ideal Schools
records.text: Thank you to Ideal Schools for supporting me through my ICB level 2 in Bookkeeping.  Ideal Schools was very quick to provide any support and advice I needed throughout.

records.title: Friendly, organised and well priced
records.text: If you're looking for a friendly, efficient and organised school to guide you through your studies, then I believe you will find it in Ideal Schools.I have been a student of the school for a number of years and have been impressed with their organisation and their warmth and friendliness whenever I have spoken to them.They have also proven to provide good value for money.

records.title: Good Provider - Level 3 AAT
records.text: My experience of Ideal was positive.  I had found them cheaper than other providers - this was the main reason i went with them.Not all modules came with separate notes, but was provided with the BPP  Workbook and Question Banks to work through.   The assignments didn't always match the chapter texts - but were always explained and marked very quickly.Tutor and Admin were very supportive.  If they did Level 4, i would have stayed with them.

records.title: Very good!
records.text: Very good provided materials and great tutorial support but sometimes felt that not all subject's theory was covered (sometimes I was surprised by questions at exams, especially in later stages). Overall teaches well how to make calculations, how to use computer system and how to pass with high score.

records.title: Material OK, tutors excellent
records.text: I felt the material was a little lacking in depth.  I qualified as CIMA several years ago and I was expecting more of that level to be honest.  The material was good, but I felt it didn't always go into enough detail for my own peace of mind - for example the computerised part of the payroll course.  It seemed to be very much "Here is how you set it up" with no explanation of why.  I appreciate that this may just be me!The tutor was very helpful, and fairly prompt in returning the assignments.

records.title: ICB Level II B1 and B2
records.text: Overall very happy with the course material and the tutor support.   There were a few things that could have made my learning smoother.  The mocks were not uptodate with the current rules regarding VAT.  Within the mock answers there was one that was wrong.  Both of these issues have been fed back to Ideal Schools but don't know whether anything will be done regarding the out of date mocks.  I learn by seeing examples so would have preferred some more complicated questions in the assignments to cover all eventualities.

records.title: Great staff
records.text: I have found the staff to always be very fast, efficient and helpful with assignments returned very quickly.  It's just a shame the course materials aren't of the same quality, although the content is great and teaches the course well there are many typing errors throughout.

records.title: An excellent quality learning partner
records.text: Hi Ideal Schools Team,With the recent completion of the ICB Career path course, I would like to take this opportunity to thank you all very much for your support over the last 11 months.  I'm sure your tuition and study materials will stand me in good stead as I diverge from my earlier management accounting career in industry and banking and try to go it alone as a bookkeeper.Aside from a couple of occasions, Ideal Schools returned my assignments and delivered new study materials timeously, and I was generally impressed with their commitment and accessibility when I did have queries.  Whilst not having any experience of other training providers in comparison, I would have no hesitation in recommending Ideal Schools as a learning partner. Keep up the good work and I wish you all the best for the future.

records.title: Ideal Schools have been great from the …
records.text: Ideal Schools have been great from the start and respond pretty quickly to any questions etc i have had. Would definitely recommend.

records.title: pleased I chose ideal schools
records.text: Brian has been extremely helpful and very knowledgable. I would recommend ideal schools because of Brian

records.title: Very
records.text: Very, very helpful staff. Would always call back when I had a query and happy to discuss everything.

records.title: Level II Bookkeeping
records.text: Really helpful tutorial support.  Very patient and provided lots of encouragement.

records.title: Good support on Payroll following difficulties
records.text: UPDATEI have since had a better experience and found the support more in line, so am upgrading the review.I have to say, unfortunately, I have had a much more underwhelming experience with the Payroll Diploma which did not quite parallel with the experience I have had with the Bookkeeping courses.I have found a few faults:1. The answers are unknown only to one member of staff whose contact is sporadic meaning I have to wait for some time to get any feedback which does not complement when I can get this work done2. I was sent notes in January but not advised of any changes until I was unaware I had incorrectly answered an assignment, making me nervous for my up and coming exam unless I re-read the entire content. The changes concerned were effective November the previous year as well, I have since discovered.3. The feedback process has been rather vague and I feel I have had no real coaching and instead have relied in the majority on looking up answers on various websites and trial-and-error. I am not sure other than the old notes I have been sent as to whether I have really received any tuition at all.My overriding impression is that Payroll as a subject matter has been bolted on to mirror the ICB syllabus and that they are under-resourced in this area.The team are great and helpful, but unfortunately the service here has not left me feeling too pleased. When I have received feedback, more often than not I have been at a real loss and left stumped with no offer to discuss or consult further, when I have really needed it. Tuition on this area has felt elusive to me.I anxiously sit the Self Assessment exams after this and hope it's more of a blip than anything else. I question know as to whether my prior positive experience was because I have much more experience in bookkeeping and in a subject where I am a little more raw, I have been let down.

records.title: Tutors not approachable
records.text: Found tutors to be unhelpful and sometimes rude despite other reviews raving about how supportive they were, maybe I was just unlucky

records.title: I felt that there was a lack of examples in the course
records.text: I am someone who like to see a lot of worked through examples before I tackle a question. I felt that this course in particular lacked examples.   Also there was one question in task that was incorrect and I spent along time trying to make my answer fit with the question.   I did speak to the tutor about this and they were very helpful and did admit that the wording of the question was wrong.

records.title: assignment delays !!!
records.text: overall fine , only problems were assignments getting lost  and extreme delays in marking assignments not even close to the 48 hours they say,, even waited a week for some.. Course material was complicated  on some stages. lack of examples,  sometimes topics were not clear . but overall not at all regretting .

records.title: So-so
records.text: The explanation of Tutors is usually insufficient, not clear and negligent.

records.title: Unhelpful
records.text: Unhelpful, old fashioned traditional examples .No help with software

records.title: Dont waste your money, worst experiance of my life!
records.text: Having searched lots of different learning providers for my L3 payroll course I decided to go with Ideal Schools based of the sales pitch they gave me on the phone offering outstadning tutor support and great course materials...well this was very far from the truth, I had countless mistakes in my course materials, delays in contact from tutor both of which I was given a guilt trip excuse about personal issues. I even had revison notes marked incorrectly and when new materials were sent to me there were still errors. And when I asked for some specifit help I was told to reffer to the course materials....well clearly I already had but they wernt giving me enough information!!! I ended up pretty much self teaching and gaining tutor support else where Ideal Schools did nothing but give excuses like the tutor had alot of marking to do or oops our mistake they pretty much washed their hands of me absolutly appauling go with someone else and save yourself the stress and angziety I had.

records.title: Dreadful service
records.text: Dreadful service. The worst.

description:
Welcome to the College of Media and Publishing. We're so pleased you found us!

There are significant advantages by studying at a genuine online college that is fully accredited, quality endorsed and registered by the UK government.

Whether you want to learn new skills at home or develop your career at work, our online courses are acclaimed as among the best on the market, and lead to endorsed certificates.

Our accredited online courses have been running since 2003 are trusted by more than 300 organisations, including Arsenal FC, The BBC, BT, Disney, John Lewis, The NHS, Vodafone, Virgin Media and Waitrose. They are also used by thousands of individuals who want to change careers, get jobs or set up their own freelance businesses.

You will benefit from unlimited, personal support from an expert tutor, including in-depth feedback on your assignments, and expert careers advice.

Our easy to use Online Learning Area makes studying simple. You can fit your course around your lifestyle, and learn at a pace that suits you, without the pressure of deadlines.
Our popular courses:

Business writing (QLS Level 4)
Copywriting (QLS Level 4)
Google SEO (QLS Level 4)
Proofreading and copy editing (QLS Level 4) 
SEO content writing course (QLS Level 4)
Social media marketing (QLS Level 4)

records.title: Excellent copywriting course
records.text: The copywriting course exceeded my expectations. It took around 6 months for me to complete the course around my full time job. I liked being able to complete the lessons and assignments at my own pace. My tutor, Elena always responded very quickly and provided useful feedback. I have learnt so much through this course and feel more confident with my copywriting skills as a result.

records.title: Very helpful assistants
records.text: Very helpful assistants - friendly advice and clear information given. I have not started my course yet but I feel confident that I will receive the support I need to accomplish my goals.

records.title: The clarity of the learning material.
records.text: The clarity of the learning material, including the multiple links to relevant articles, was invaluable. My excellent tutor gave me positive and honest feedback and always turned around an assignment in super quick time. Thank you!

records.title: Proofreading and editing course
records.text: I have just completed the Proofreading and Editing course. A great experience! It highly exceeded my expectations!Already a copyeditor and proofreader of Spanish texts, I wanted to broaden my horizons, and English is a language I love since I was a child. After examining different alternatives, I chose CMP and this course.  The course contents covered the different points of the syllabus with complete and up-to-date information, including recommendations of books and links to different kinds of external sources, some of which, in time, led to other sources. Some of the lessons, in fact, were kind of fascinating trips to me. I really enjoyed going through them. And the practical assignments were always challenging. It was great that, no matter how many errors or other situations I could find in them, there was always something else to be noticed! I really liked that.The tutorial support was also noteworthy. Julian always provided corrections, as well as respectful and enriching feedbacks, in a timely manner.  And just as remarkable was the student experience support provided by Olly and Jake.I have equipped myself with highly useful skills and in a comfortable environment. I warmly recommend it!

records.title: Copywriting course
records.text: My tutor Lucy was very helpful and also replied promptly to my coursework enquiries.I found the course itself very informative, and the College of Media and Publishing staff were friendly.Overall good value for money too.

records.title: I was really impressed with the CMP…
records.text: I really enjoyed the CMP copywriting course. As a professional editor/writer, it was a good 'reminder' of some of the basics, while picking up hints and resources along the way. I worried it might be too basic, but the assignments were challenging and fun. Practising different types of writing was really useful, and leaving the course with a ready-made portfolio was a huge bonus!My tutor always responded within three business days with thoughtful feedback. It was both a confidence boost and a great way to learn how to improve.It's a lot of self-directed work, but that was clear from the start. At the very least, I was able to do it in my own time - hugely helpful on top of a full-time job.I'd highly recommend this course to anyone starting or advancing a career in copywriting (especially as a qualification boost) - it's a practical, hands-on programme for all kinds of writers.

records.title: Comprehensive, up-to-date content
records.text: Course Review: Social Media Marketing Course - College of Media and Publishing⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐I recently completed the Social Media Marketing Course with the College of Media and Publishing, and I am extremely satisfied with the experience. The course is well-structured, easy to follow, and covers a comprehensive range of topics that are essential for mastering social media marketing.What I appreciated most about the course was how practical and up-to-date the content was. It didn’t just focus on theory; there were real-world examples and case studies which helped me understand how to apply the strategies. I especially found the modules on content creation, analytics, and platform-specific strategies incredibly useful.The online format was user-friendly, and I liked that I could learn at my own pace while still having access to support from the tutors. The learning materials were clear, and there were interactive quizzes that helped reinforce my understanding.One constructive suggestion I’d offer is for the course to include more detailed insights into paid advertising strategies across platforms like Facebook and Instagram, as this is a key area for many businesses. But overall, I feel this course has equipped me with the knowledge and confidence to implement social media marketing strategies effectively.If you’re looking to enhance your skills in social media marketing, I highly recommend this course. It’s an excellent investment for anyone wanting to build a career or grow a business online.Pros:Comprehensive, up-to-date contentPractical, real-world examplesSelf-paced with tutor supportClear and easy-to-understand materials

records.title: I am a single mum with part time work…
records.text: I am a single mum with part time work and part time online uni. I needed something to spruce up my writing and editing skills. I haven't gone through the entire course but i have received my very first bigger mark already. Happy is an understatement!

records.title: Great learning experience
records.text: As an assistant, part of my job involves proofreading and editing documents. I enrolled in this course to enhance these skills and eventually find part-time work as a proofreader. I'm glad I did. I have learned so much.  Thanks to my tutor, Shuna Meade, for her patience and guidance.

records.title: Great course with a supportive tutor
records.text: I thoroughly enjoyed the Copywriting course, the CMP tutor was supportive throughout. I love the fact that you can study at your own pace, and your tutor is there if you have any questions. I'm a little sad that it's over - out into the real world I go!

records.title: My blogging course experience
records.text: I really enjoyed doing my blogging course through the College of Media and Publishing. The course was well-structured and very useful. The pace of each lesson was easy to follow. My tutors gave me valuable feedback after each assignment that helped me improve my understanding of concepts and shape my blogging writing style. Thank you! The tutors were also easy to get hold of and very helpful if I had any questions.

records.title: A satisfying course overall
records.text: Overall, the course was good & well thought through. The lessons were interesting, up to date & easy to follow. My tutor was very quick at marking assignments, which I appreciated as I could then continue with the course at my pace. I really appreciated the fact that there was no time constraint on completing this course, making it very flexible & easy to fit in around other commitments.While I appreciated my tutor's speed at marking assignments, & the feedback that he gave, I didn't find his responses to my queries very helpful. This was disappointing, as I was hoping for more constructive tutor interaction, which would have aided/enhanced my learning.I also would have liked to have a final marked assignment, as the end of the course felt a little flat & dampened the sense of achievement at completing it.So, there could be some improvements, but I'm glad I took the course & have definitely learnt from it.

records.title: I recently undertook a proofreading and…
records.text: I recently undertook a proofreading and editing course. It wasn't too bad, though certain modules could be tricky enough. It certainly gave me an understanding to proofreading and editing for certain types of work.

records.title: Great learning experience…
records.text: I found the course a great and very flexible learning experience. My tutor Justine Holman, was just fantastic. She made me enjoy the work and encouraged me to complete the course in the face of some health challenges, offering me great and constructive advice. The assignments were always marked in a timely manner and sometimes earlier than I expected to give myself some breathing space before taking on the next!It was hard work at times but fun and engaging. Equipped with copywriting skills I now have a whole new world before me in addition to my journalism. I would like to do proofreading with them next.

records.title: SEO content writing - a great learning experience
records.text: I liked everything about the search engine optimization (SEO) content writing course. It is well structured with good material in both text and video format. I felt motivated from start to finish and the assignments were marked up in good time. The college offers a good range of media and publishing related courses, and I've already signed up for two more.

records.title: Value for money
records.text: I very much enjoyed the Copyediting and Proofreading course with CMP. It covered a good range of topics and gave valuable advice on finding and working with clients. The tutor feedback was extensive. I found the online learning portal to be a little dated and the formatting rules very strict, but this was also a good practice of the attention to detail required in this line of work. All in all a good experience, which I am already putting into practice!

records.title: The lessons were great
records.text: The lessons were great, very informative, and well-structured. My tutor Shauna was fantastic and she responded to every question. However, what this course lacks is a link to the actual working world. There is a section on "Finding Work", but the information is too general. They should offer tutoring or shadowing, i.e. the opportunity to work with a proofreader in real time for a real project. Also maybe there should create referral links to certain agencies for those who get above a certain grade.

records.title: A really useful SEO content course
records.text: The SEO content writing course was really useful. I'm already a professional copywriter, and this filled a lot of gaps in my SEO knowledge.A few of the modules would benefit from an update, and a couple were a little obscure, one or two over-long, but overall I'd highly recommend the course content.The tutor support was outstanding — a super-fast turnaround with valuable feedback that all made perfect sense — and the college was efficient throughout.

records.title: Useful and informative
records.text: The course content was excellent and comprehensive, thank you. Customer service was efficient and response time was fast. My tutor might have been a little more encouraging and helpful in his replies. My successes were acknowledged but I didn't feel supported during the one lesson when I was struggling desperately to get to grips with a completely new concept. I got there in the end but had thought I would never grasp or understand what I was being asked to do.

records.title: Feed me in gently
records.text: It is taking me some time to get into the course especially the use of web pages and the huge amount of material to take in, recall and apply.  There is a lot of ambiguity within the 'rules' overall.There is a load of digital info on the RHS of the screen as I write which is of no use to me and is a distraction!

records.title: A great start
records.text: I enjoyed this learning experience. I was able to study on my own timeframe and found the multi-choice quizzes to be a good indicator of materials I needed to review again to ensure I had a good grasp of the subject matter. The tutor's comments were patient and helpful. This course was a great introduction to proofreading and I feel confident in moving ahead to freelance work.

records.title: Almost perfect
records.text: The tests are good and really drill the information in well. Responses are good from the tutors and I love how I can do this at my own pace, I feel like I'm learning a lot.There were a couple of instances though where questions on the test did not have the information in the lesson so I was trying to answer question on information I had not been given. Other than that a very good service.

records.title: I would recommend CMP to anyone
records.text: I've just completed the web writing course and have thoroughly enjoyed it. You are very much on your own in many online courses. I like that every CMP module ends with an assignment which has to be completed and marked by a tutor. You also cannot start a new module unless you have passed, which stops you from skimming through to tick the boxes and get the certification. As for Ian Campbell, my tutor, he was thorough and always there to help.  CMP to get on

records.title: Great experience!
records.text: I recently completed the proofreading and editing course with CMP, and I was very impressed. There were a variety of modules that I learnt a lot from, and my tutor responded to my messages and marked my assignments promptly—sometimes, not even within a day of uploading them. The feedback was fair and helpful, and there were a couple of optional modules that you could complete if you wanted to (proofreading on paper and fiction editing). These were self-marked.Agreeing with someone else's comment, I wouldn't say that I'm currently qualified to seek a job in proofreading and editing. There's a lot more for me to learn, especially since I want to go into fiction editing, which was an optional module that I didn't receive feedback for. It's a great baseline, though. I'd definitely consider completing more courses with CMP in future. Thank you for the great experience!

records.title: Proofreading course was not for me
records.text: I would give my tutor, Shuna Meade, 5 stars for her support and encouragement throughout. However, I feel that 2 weeks is not sufficient time to decide whether the course is right for you. After successfully submitting three assignments, but struggling with the fourth, I realised that this course was not for me. I was hoping this course would enable me to earn additional income but instead I have lost the money I invested, as they give you just two weeks to change your mind. Two weeks is not enough time to make an informed decision.Addendum: further to your response and offer of additional help, I am not able to apply myself to the course for various reasons, but do appreciate your offer, and that of Shuna.

records.title: informative, practical, stimulating and enjoyable
records.text: The course was informative, practical, stimulating and enjoyable. Assignments were always promptly marked, and those graded by a tutor were bespoke. It wasn't easy for me to find 1:1 support, but it's there if you look carefully inside an array of information, or just ask. Since completing the proofreading course, I've been directed to CMP's career coaching course, which I've just started.

records.title: The tasks explained very well
records.text: The tasks explained very well. Variety of activities to do in many of the lessons.Well explained theoretical work.

records.title: Fantastic course
records.text: Fantastic course! Lots of focussed assignments that take you through the basics of copywriting and get you writing. My tutor was responsive and helpful, and her feedback was invaluable to me improving as the course progressed. I would definitely recommend anyone taking the course if you're looking to improve your writing skills or are looking to start down the road of freelancing.The only negative (which takes my mark down to 4 stars) is that there is no phone support at all - all questions and queries are conducted via an online portal. The responses are quick, so not a problem for the majority of queries but there were an occasion or two where I waited for a couple of days for an answer to a query that would have been answered with a short call, there and then. However, this isn't too much of a concern for me - I have already booked another course with CMP!

records.title: Great tutor and excellent learning material
records.text: I took the Creative Copywriting course online and it was one of the best decisions!You have full flexibility in the pace of learning and my tutor Justine was very helpful and constructive in her feedback. She really guided me to understand and apply different techniques when writing. Upon completion of the course, I’ve gained a lot of confidence and it elevated my career as a content manager.

records.title: The Level 4 copywriting course is…
records.text: The Level 4 copywriting course is incredible value for money compared to other courses I looked at. There was a wealth of information provided over a well-structured and manageable 20-lesson programme. My online tutor was very personable, provided plenty of constructive and in-depth feedback and marked my assignments efficiently allowing me to crack on with the next module. And it doesn't just end when the last lesson is completed as I was provided with a load of practical information on how to start obtaining work afterwards. I considered just diving into freelance copywriting but I'm so glad I took this course first as I feel so much better prepared now.

records.title: Generally good but some inconsistencies
records.text: I found the information provided directly by CMP to be well written & clear. Unfortunately they sometimes provide a link to third party instructions (for example Adobe Acrobat) and I found that information unclear & difficult to understand - I would prefer CMP to precis such information & include it in their own scripts.

records.title: It taught me the basics...
records.text: I did the proofreading and editing course and it wasn't a bad course. The parts it did cover were done well and since I got the course on a discount I can say that I got my money's worth, but, it wasn't very thorough. After I got my certificates and started looking for work I realized that I wasn't really qualified to be a proofreader or editor. It's not the full price worth and you're going to have to do some extra learning on your own if for example you want to be able to do proofreading and editing for creative writing, something I felt the course lacked (a lot). But I don't regret doing the course even if I only got the basics.

records.title: Will teach you some general things about journalism and writing articles
records.text: I found the course as a whole quite helpful (in terms of learning some general things about journalism and getting some practice). I think that the tutor's feedback was helpful, even though it wasn't very detailed (it's not like you'll learn how to write good articles just by doing this course). If you're interested in journalism in general (and don't know much about it), the course is helpful. If you're interested in something specific, like writing for women's magazines, then you won't get much out of it. Also, it's all based on the UK (the examples, laws, rules, sources, etc.). Many links are outdated (examples of articles from more than ten years ago) or not accessible anymore. This should be updated.Edit (reply): I don't know how that's possible because I bought this course last year, so in 2021.

records.title: Trustworthy. Professional. Proficient
records.text: The learning experience with CMP has been a positive one. And my journey with them continues as I develop my skillset in writing. Their knowledge base is sound, and they are trustworthy and professional. The learning platform they use is rudimentary but it does what it needs to.If you are looking for a starting point to gain qualifications in the realms of writing, media and publishing, CMP is a good place to start place.

records.title: I find it all very awkward to navigate…
records.text: I find it all very awkward to navigate around - not as user friendly as I would have hoped

records.title: Tutor assistance
records.text: I didn't find the reply from my tutor to a query I made very helpful.  In fact it was no help at all.

records.title: Not enough learning for the price
records.text: The course tutor Justine was good, however I found the course material to be too basic and not challenging enough. I felt I could have learned a lot more for the price paid, and certainly one of the resources was out of date (this was confirmed by Justine and will be removed for future courses). I'm glad it came with a recognised qualification, which was why I did the course, and I did learn a few things I hadn't known before. However even at 50% off I found the course to be very overpriced.

records.title: I loved the materials (they are really…
records.text: I loved the materials (they are really really good). 5 stars!My tutor was very nice but I wish we had had more interaction. Asking questions was not easy (the interface you use is not user-friendly). I also wish we had access to the materials before having the corrections. Sometimes you have time and you do want to work on the course, but it's not possible, because you must wait for 3 days. R.H. was not very professional: most of my messages were not answered. I insist, though: your materials are very good.

records.title: I didn't realize there was a time limit…
records.text: I didn't realize there was a time limit to completing the course.  I think this should be 'red-flagged' big box, very clearly stated so that other people like me don't pay for the course, get unfortunate life events and are not able to complete within the time period.

records.title: I'm enjoying learning what the course…

records.title: My thoughts on CMP are as follows:
records.text: My thoughts on CMP are as follows:•	Undoubtably, I did learn a decent amount about proofreading and editing.•	The materials presented were generally of decent quality (although quite a lot of what I learned was by reading external materials which the course provided links to).•	The course was of a significantly lower cost than some of the alternatives.However, on the less positive side:•	I think the course is cheaper because at the end of the day, you get less out of it by comparison to other courses – it is at a much higher level (i.e. it goes into less depth)•	CMP do an excellent job of marketing – in fact at times I found it too aggressive – and I’ve had to exchange several emails to get myself removed from their mailing lists.•	One of their key sales pitches was the availability of an individual who could answer any question.   I found this to be useful, but only in a very limited sense.   The course material is relatively simple and you don’t really need to ask many questions to pass the course.•	I was delighted to pass the course with a “distinction” only to find that literally everyone passes the course with distinction.  It’s another example I think of CMP’s marketing strategy…make students feel good about the course to get better feedback on SM.•	The biggest gap I found was in the final section – how to get a job.    There was undoubtedly some bits of useful advice here, but the reality is that it’s very hard to find work in this industry.   It’s my understanding (I may be wrong) that competitor courses offer more tangible help to get work for students.   I short I would say this course is fine if you acknowledge up-front that you will just be learning the basics, and you’re going to need to spend more money later to do more learning / more networking.

records.title: Cheap and Cheerful.
records.text: This review is based on my early experiences, and I have only completed the first lesson.  However, first impressions are important.The content is OK, but the first 'assignment' was a quiz which bore little relation to the content I had studied and researched, as per the first lesson.I have also not had any contact from my 'Tutor' yet, but still get bombarded with emails from this College trying to sell me new courses.    Cheap and cheerful.**UPDATE**  Further to the reply to this review, I am responding here as the College, despite being able to send me countless sales emails, have yet to contact me to address the concerns I have posted here. So, I am left with no choice but to respond to their reply here, on a public review forum.   I have been designing and delivering adult training programmes for 20 years.  The purpose of (formative) assessment should be to help embed the learning.  This first 'assignment' was not an assignment at all, but a multiple choice quiz. Whilst quizzes can be an effective method of formative assessment, it certainly wasn't the written assigment I was expecting, as per the wording in the course material. Nor did it cover what I felt were the  points from the first lesson.  As for contact with my tutor - the College state that tutors will contact students when their first assignment has been submitted.  I am still waiting to be contacted.  A simple 'welcome' email from my tutor would have sufficed.

records.title: AKT practice papers pitched at much too hard a level with poor question format generally.
records.text: I cannot comment on any other aspect of Arora training, only the AKT papers I purchased.With regards to the 5 AKT revision papers -  The average scores for these papers for over all users is 50.58%, 51.85%, 57.81%, 49.63%, 39.49%. This is very revealing.Frustratingly, I have taken the AKT 3 times scoring 70% 68.5% and 69.5%, so I am well aware of the difficulty level of the exam itself.These papers, while perhaps useful for general, training are not pitched at the right level for AKT revision in my opinion. Many require nuanced or more specialist knowledge, rather than ST3 or newly-qualified GP-level knowledge.  Many of the questions are written in the format of ''which is the least accurate statement'' which can be very confusing.  I would *estimate* that 50-70% of the questions are in this format, at least. There were very few graphical or table-based questions, no extended matching questions in the exams I took, and no image questions in the papers I took.More than once the answers to questions was contradicted in the explanations to other questions in later sections of the paper or on another paper, I noted.  Not frequent, but certainly occured.While it is useful to be challenged, personally I would advise an alternative revision source before paying £87 for and using this AKT paper bundle. It was quite a demoralising experience, even if I have picked up some more medicine from it.

records.title: The Digital College course was…please read
records.text: The Digital College course was interesting and well presented although some tutorial notes to download would have been helpful. Not being able to complete the exam immediately after the training - 5 days to wait for first exam slot- was not helpful. If I had known this before starting the course I would of planned appropriately. Take note of emails going to your spam box - mine did.I had to enlist tech support to set up to take the exam (online at home) as the process isn’t simple. However the invigilator help desk was extremely supportive.

records.title: Does the job but slowly
records.text: The course is delivered by instructional video, and there are no written notes so you have to laboriously write down everything yourself - it would be so much better if you were given the power point slides / transcripts or notes to review / copy as it is so much faster to read than to re-watch the videos. In summary, this is the slowest way to learn - if you're looking for slow then great. But if you want to get the course done as quickly as possible, this will take the longest.The technology is a bit clunky - feels quite outdatedThe power points are quite boring. But all the information is there

records.title: Mostly good with room for improvement
records.text: Having used Learndirect before I bought another course CBT LV 5. The course content seemed acceptable and I loved the no time limited aspect. Due to a lengthy break I was removed from my course and told it didn't exist. After hours of circular argument with an agent, I requested the schools regulator. The agent refused to tell me or address my issues. I ended up going through a complaint process, confusingly referred to as a feedback form. The first complaint handler referred it onto the/a resolution manager Jess. Jess was very professional in her initial response filling me with some redeemed confidence that I would be heard and treated fairly. The complaint had several points that were all addressed and a resolution was made for me to continue my course with the admin fee set out in my original terms and conditions. While I am very grateful, I can't help but also be annoyed, remembering the first agent who not only refused to honour the T's&C's but telling me the course doesn't exist. Having now paid the re-enrolment fee, I have restarted my course. Accessing the content had some minor issues due to a system migration but this was very quickly resolved by another agent.Getting in touch with Learndirect is very easy by phone or live chat but the quality of agents and their information can vary drastically.As my course will take some time, I will follow up with a final review on its completion.I am reasonably happy with Learndirect though I would shop around other providers for future learning.

records.title: Level 4 Diploma in Canine Welfare, Training and Behaviour
records.text: I had a challenging time during this course as I found it an extensive course to try and balance alongside work. The learning material was presented in the format of a workbook to read and assessment's to answer following. The assessments were very time consuming and some questions felt repetitive which made me feel like I was making slow progress. I would have appreciated a mix of learning materiel, such as videos and interactive activities, to further support learning. The communication throughout the course was very poor. However, my experience over the last few months has been amazing with my new tutor Sienna Taylor. She made such a difference to my learning and confidence by simplifying bits that I found complicated and being easily contactable. Her support was very encouraging and motivating. I think my whole experience of the course would have been much improved if I had Sienna as a tutor from the start. I enjoyed the range of units and particularly enjoyed learning through cases studies.

records.title: Dont book maths with LearnDirect Book with Pass Functional Skills instead
records.text: I personally didn't have a good experience. I signed up as needed evidence of my L2 Maths. I paid for the full course and exam. I initially asked to do installments on my credit card and was told this was fine. The following month I was locked out of my revision profile. I was then told I had to set up a direct debit (which I did) only to continue to be locked out every month for the next 3 months. I spent long periods on the chat function, phone and email trying to get my account reopened and show proof that the money had come out of my account.I wrote a formal complaint after the third time my account was closed. I recieved no apology, no explanation they just reopened my account. I noticed not long after they removed the instant chat function completely. The video's and resources had a few errors which is unprofessional and not helpful to someone trying to learn.The tutor support minimal, simply telling you to refer back to the study materials.The "live" sessions were copies of the videos  already in the study materials.I would recommend pass functional skills over learn direct as they have better resources that are free and when you book an exam with them they send you 2 mock papers and formula sheets to memorise.

records.text: What a great experience. Having been a supporter of IOSCM for several years now I have to say the institute is doing a great job of keeping the industry moving forward. records.title: It was a fantastic event.

records.title: Another excellent well delivered event…

records.title: I'm nearly half way through my course
records.text: I'm nearly half way through my course, so far it has been straight forward to follow and my tutor is easily contactable. Given the busy nature of my current role this course allows me to tackle each module at my own pace to fit around my role. Looking forward to completing my second half of the course.

records.title: recently started with IOSCM everything…

records.title: Excellent night to celebrate many successes

records.title: A good study for improving supply chain management at the managerial level

However, it is easy to contact to instructors in case there is a question.It is perfect challenge if you like doing self-study. It requires a big dedication and serious amount of detailed study.

records.title: Easy Access For Learners
records.text: I've recently started a level 5 diploma in transport and logistics, along with leadership skills and business management. records.title: The enrolling process was really easy…

records.title: I have just completed my course with…

records.title: My experience during the course journey
records.text: I appreciated the content and quality of courses, the platform structure and the rigour of tutors regarding the contents of the assignments submission. On the other side, I didn't appreciate the time taken for feedback. I think 10 open working days is too much.

records.title: It was nice to learn about logistics…
records.text: It was nice to learn about logistics through course. The book that was provided was easy to read and easy to understand which was beneficial to me when I was doing my assignments. When I had questions, I got a quick response from the institution which I am happy with.

records.title: Intensive, but good.
records.text: Enrolling it was very easy. The the first steps were very well explained, and phone calls received when I  when I struggled. records.title: So far so good

records.title: Early days but all good

records.title: Great training company
records.text: Great training company. I found this company through google search for courses and found the range of courses to fit my requirements. records.title: Course content and platform is overall…

records.title: Overall positive experience (thus far!)
records.text: Firstly I came here to write a review as I was emailed by Ioscm with the promise of a voucher for completing a review :-) so here I am. I shall report back here if it’s not! I’m optimistic that all will be ok. I too agree with others that I think the system could be configured in a more user friendly way and multiple platforms are a headache. I struggled slightly navigating the system but managed. records.title: I am still in the beginning stages of…

records.title: Level 3 diploma

records.title: Second course with IOSCM

records.title: Overwhelm experience with the Institute

records.title: Good Course
records.text: I like that you can mix and match your different units. I do think the online platform could be much easier to navigate and a clearer explanation of submission expectations could be issued at the beginning.The platform induction was detailed but I have found the content easy to forget.The need to write in the word counts on the assignments is very easy to overlook and miss and wasn't shown to me as a requirement in my induction. it would be useful to be reminded of this and have it as a highlighted factor on the templates.As a learner who can get bored very easily, I need a combination of learning styles so at the moment, I have found the course content to be intense as it is mostly factual text and not many pictures or interactive videos. This would definitely improve the enjoyment and accessibility of the course.Overall the course content is comprehensive and the need to complete your own research at level 5 is crucial. If your completing at level 5 or higher, its worth practicing the Harvard Referencing too as this is very confusing if you haven't done it before.

records.title: Pros and Cons of the level 5 SCM course
records.text: I am currently studying the level 5 Supply chain management course and I am 4 months in, here are some pros and cons I've found so far:Pros: - plenty of choice for different modules, even though I chose a 'Supply chain management' course, there was plenty of interesting options outside this such as project management and leadership modules- Quick marking turn arounds so I know whether I was on the right path for my first assignment Cons- Information varied from email queries to the induction q&a on word counts- Very limited feedback from how to get from a 'good pass' to an 'excellent pass'. Feedback was very vague and not particular useful- Poor response times from tutor over email and had to chase- No in person reviews

records.title: Needs modernising
records.text: The essay titles are somewhat engaging but I have found nothing useful on the learning resource hub, no connection with other students, the study guide seems to have pulled information from various sources and so reads very clunky. The suggested bibliography is quite out of date. The platform is not user friendly. There is no guidance/support for using online academic resources or how to make appropriate use of AI. When I asked for a tutor phone call I was offered a call days away at 6.30am which is completely impractical. I have found the course a bit of a slog without human interaction. Perhaps that is just me. It is a reasonably accessible course that is flexible enough to fit around work if you can manage it. I would just like a more modern experience.

records.title: For the most part it's been easy to…
records.text: For the most part it's been easy to use, well supported courses I've done through IoSCM. I did a level 5 that was great, no issues. Good information, well supported. The platform changed without my knowledge so I've done essays that are now pointless as the learning objectives have changed for the modules I was half way through. Hours of wasted work. I have been given a free 3 month extension but still annoying. Most tutors are fine. One tutor i have though calls from outside of the UK and the barrier in language made my tutor call completely pointless and I gained zero benefit or constructive guidance from them. description:
Established in 1994, Sensory Integration Education  is a not-for-profit organisation working with allied health professionals, education and health experts, academic researchers and families to improve awareness, understanding and the treatment of sensory integration and sensory processing difficulties.
We do all this using the proven framework of Ayres Sensory Integration Therapy. For over 30 years and in over 100 countries, we have trained those who work with and care for people with sensory challenges. We support and disseminate research into Ayres Sensory Integration Therapy.
Our MSc in Sensory Integration pathway, delivering SI Practitioner and Advanced Practitioner status, was the world’s first postgraduate qualification in SI accredited by a UK university. Our higher education partner is Sheffield Hallam University, one of the UK's largest education providers for allied health professions. Find out more about our partnership here.
Our Lifelong Learning Programme is a trusted companion for professionals and therapists, supporting and informing them with expertise and live peer support.
We are proud to be a not-for-profit organisation that invests surpluses into course development and supports early-career researchers. We encourage, support, and disseminate research into Ayres Sensory Integration Therapy. 
PLEASE NOTE: Our company, Sensory Integration Education, is in no way affiliated with 'Sensory Education' (website: www. cheap disability aids. co .uk) PLEASE CHECK THAT YOU ARE LEAVING A REVIEW FOR THE CORRECT COMPANY. Thank you.

records.title: Fantastic
records.text: I have loved my experience of learning with Sensory Integration Education. I have completed my PGDip and am now in my last year of the Masters with Sheffield Hallam, but realised I don't think I have ever left a review before!A fantastic, professional and transparent organisation that supports people to develop into autonomous and creative practitioners. There is no one I'd rather have trained with.Thank you for the learning and for the incredible community that I am proud to be a part of.

records.title: This course has opened my mind to certain basic behaviors that are linked to sensor difficulty and how to help manage such individuals positively.
records.text: The whole course is designed very simple and impactful. I support people with different kinds of sensory difficulties, eg dyspraxia, fluctuating sensory, delayed processing, light, and touch, etc. The company has done a great job by helping support workers who enrolled in this course to be able to manage individuals with sensory difficulties. Most importantly, You made us understand that their actions and behaviors are not something they can control. It has to do with Sensory difficulties.

records.title: The course was informative
records.text: The course was informative. I enjoyed it the lay out of the video and notes made it easy to follow. This also assisted my understanding of the topic.I like that the terms and definitions given came with suggestions and examples.

records.title: Understanding and be more supportive to the adult with learning disabilities
records.text: This is so interesting and more educative. This has given me more incite on how to understand the people with learning difficulties better and be more supportive to them

records.title: A great  conference with a variety of…
records.text: A great  conference with a variety of speaker and topics from infants to older adults.  Learned many things that I knew nothing about.  The international perspective was so helpful in learning new things.  Easy to get the presentations though some did not offer the ppt for participants.  Even the posters were helpful to hear the authors talk about their research!  Thank you for offering this conference for free.

records.text: The presentation is very clear, one can access for 30 days which is really convenient and is possible to read the transcription of the audio/video, even download it. Some information could be basic but still is useful. Thank you

records.title: New experience.
records.text: Hi, I'm new to your platform. My name is Thomas, I come from Poland, and I am a swimming coach and teacher in Norwegian schools. I have been living in Norway for over 17 years, working and developing here. Thanks to water, I can observe how it affects my students with various problems. I also have children on the autism spectrum. I see the progress they are making. Thanks to your platform, I can make parents aware of the wonderful effects of water on children and how to handle children sensitive to external stimuli. It's amazing that you have appeared on my life's horizon. Thank you very much.

records.title: It has provided me with valuable…
records.text: It has provided me with valuable insights and introduced ideas that have opened new perspectives for my work with students.

records.title: I liked knowing the breakdown of each module and how long it’ll take to complete the course
records.text: I liked knowing how to get the certificate. I’m not sure if this the platform to ask but I’m in South Africa and wondering how the hours and costs would work for me? Especially if there’s online discussions…

records.title: A short and brief, but informative free course
records.text: The free course about SI was brief but informative. It was basic, but had a few golden nuggets of information.

records.text: It was easy to listen to but not engaging.Frustrating that there is no educational experienced route into Sensory Integration.Thank you for your reply. I will have a look at your sister site.

records.title: Fantastic course
records.text: Fantastic course, would have valued more information on intervention although acknowledge that interoception is a new area.

records.title: The session was very informative
